about: Own-words paraphrases of the GECK wiki page of each base-game script function (origin GECK1, VEGAS1, CONSOLENV), written 2026-10-07 from the private Special:Export dump. Tag: [documented] (source: the linked wiki page). bugs = original-engine quirks the page reports. No sentence is copied from the wiki; keep it that way when editing.

functions.summary: Takes a float and returns its absolute value; not called on a reference.
Triggers the activation event of the calling object, optionally naming the activating reference and choosing whether the script's activation block runs or default activation happens.
notes: ActionRef omitted: the calling reference's existing action ref is used; if it has none, nothing is activated.
RunOnActivateBlockFlag 0 or omitted gives default activation (NPCs start dialogue, containers and doors open, items are taken by the player) and skips the script's activation block.
Flag 1 runs the object's activation block instead of default activation and requires an ActionRef; the target script runs immediately, delaying the caller's next line.
Passing the player as argument does not activate the player; the caller is activated with the player stored as its activator.
Activating an item with an enabled NPC as activator makes that NPC pick it up, even if unconscious; containers do not.
bugs: Flag 0 on an object lacking an activation block (or any script) permanently stops normal activation of it, e.g. containers cannot be opened and NPCs cannot be talked to again.
Showing a message box in a container's activation block then activating it afterwards leaves the player stuck in an unusable inventory screen.
Activating a stacked item in an inventory with the player as activator moves one item and destroys the rest of the stack.

functions.summary: Unlocks the achievement with the given index on Steam or GFWL; takes a single integer and is not called on a reference.
notes: The page lists achievement numbers for New Vegas and its DLC (and separately for Fallout 3); index meanings come from that table.

functions.summary: Adds the calling playing card reference to the player's Caravan deck.
notes: Called on a card reference.

functions.summary: Permanently appends a creature or leveled creature to an existing leveled creature list at a given level, mainly for patching base-game lists at runtime.
notes: Arguments are the list, the creature (or leveled creature) base form, and the level at which it becomes eligible.
The change is stored in save data and cannot be reverted.
Intended for rare cases such as DLC altering base-game lists, not routine content.

functions.summary: Inserts a form at index 0 of a form list, shifting existing entries up by one; the change is baked into the save.
notes: Adding a form already present just moves it to the front rather than duplicating it.
Any form type works, base objects and runtime-created references included; non-persistent references added are eventually purged from the list.
For ammo lists, re-adding the original base ammo afterwards restores it to the front; otherwise weapons display and default to the added ammo type.
bugs: Occasionally an edited form list is reset and the added entries vanish from the save.

functions.summary: Adds a given count of an item to the calling actor's or container's inventory, optionally suppressing the on-screen message and sound.
notes: Third parameter SilentlyAdd is optional; when nonzero no message or sound is shown.
A form list may be given instead of an item; each entry is added in the stated count.
Triggers the item's add-event script block once per item added.
On NPCs it makes them re-evaluate inventory and equip best armor and weapon.
bugs: Calling it from an effect script or an equip block makes the actor's weapon toggle between visible/usable and invisible/unusable; workaround is adding and removing a dummy item in the item's add block.
On an NPC already wearing armor with object effects, re-equipping stacks the effects each call until the armor is unequipped.

functions.summary: Adds items to an actor or container at a specified condition (health) fraction.
notes: Parameters are item, count, health percent as a float (example uses 0.85 for 85%), and optional message-hidden flag.
When the item comes from a leveled list, the given health percent overrides the list's own value.

functions.summary: Permanently adds a form to an existing leveled item list with level, count and health percent, mainly for patching base-game lists at runtime.
notes: Change persists in save data and cannot be undone.
ObjectToAdd may be a base object or another leveled item list.
In New Vegas the health parameter is scaled 0 to 100, whereas Fallout 3 used 0 to 1.

functions.summary: Adds a note to the player's notes and shows a corner message whose text comes from a game setting; not called on a reference.
notes: Message text is controlled by the sComputersAddedNote game setting.

functions.summary: Permanently adds an NPC or leveled character to an existing leveled character list at a given level, mainly for patching base-game lists at runtime.
notes: Arguments are the leveled character list, the NPC or leveled list to add, and the level.
Change persists in save data and cannot be undone.

functions.summary: Console-oriented command that creates an occlusion plane of given width and height at the camera; negative values create a portal and a lone zero clears temporary ones.
Increases a perk's rank on the calling actor by one (rank 1 if new); on the player, a nonzero teammates flag targets companions instead.
notes: Optional second parameter forTeammates (0/1) only matters when called on the player; nonzero adds to the player's separate teammate perk list.
The player holds two perk lists: one for itself, one applied to all current companions.
Perk prerequisites do not apply to companion perks; conditions such as identity checks should restrict who benefits.
When companions change, remove and re-add companion perks to force re-evaluation.
Mod-created perks left in a Fallout 3 save may crash older versions when the mod is gone (FO3).

functions.summary: Adds fame or infamy with a faction's reputation using a deed-size scale from 1 to 5.
notes: First integer picks infamy (0) or fame (1); the second integer is deed size 1 to 5.
Actual points per size come from game settings; defaults are 1, 2, 4, 7 and 12 for sizes 1 through 5.
A negative amount removes reputation but the message still reads as gained.

functions.summary: Adds an exact float amount of fame or infamy to a faction's reputation.
notes: First parameter picks infamy (0) or fame (1); second is the exact amount.
A negative amount removes reputation but the message still reads as gained.

functions.summary: Gives the calling actor a script package that overrides all other packages until it finishes.
notes: An actor holds only one script package; a second call replaces the first.
Without must-complete or must-reach-location constraints, the package is dropped at the next package re-evaluation.
Affects only that actor reference, not other references or the base form.
The added package is saved with the game.
bugs: A package added from inside a dialogue result script might not get attached to the speaker.

functions.summary: Opens the character-generation Attributes page so the player can distribute a given number of extra SPECIAL points, implemented via an attribute override.
notes: While the menu is open, SPECIAL values cannot be lowered below their base values.
If the points cannot all be spent (all stats already at maximum), the menu cannot be exited.

functions.summary: Gives the calling actor an actor effect (spell, ability or addiction in vanilla) that applies immediately.
notes: On non-unique actors the effect lands on the base object, so references spawned later from it also carry the effect.

functions.summary: Opens the character-generation Skills page letting the player tag a given number of extra skills.
notes: Initial tagged skills cannot be un-tagged in this menu state.
At most four tagged skills take effect; extra picks beyond four are ignored, also via SetTagSkills.

functions.summary: Puts the specific calling actor reference into a faction at the given rank.
notes: Affects only the reference, unlike SetFactionRank which affects the base form.

functions.summary: Appends a dialogue topic to another topic's add-topic list, giving that topic an extra selectable choice.
notes: Intended for dialogue result scripts only.
Using the editor's add-topic list instead is not merged between mods, so scripting is more compatible.

functions.summary: Increments the player's character level and brings up the level-up menu.
Moves the calling actor up or down a number of age steps within its race chain, swapping it to the older or younger linked race.
notes: Positive values age the actor, negative values make it younger, each step following the race's older/younger links; overshooting clamps at the oldest or youngest available.
Only races with linked age variants are affected; in Fallout 3 only the human races have them, with child, adult and old stages (FO3).
The actor takes the default face textures of the new race; invalid hair falls back to default, restored on return for the player only.
Younger-then-older does not reliably return to the original race since links need not be symmetric or already-child values are ignored.

functions.summary: Toggles whether the calling actor's dialogue subtitles are always displayed (0 off, 1 on).
notes: The setting is not saved and resets every time a game is loaded.

functions.summary: Plays the given imagespace modifier as a screen effect.
notes: The blood imagespace modifier is apparently unused in the release data; the screen-blood function is the proper way to show blood.

functions.summary: Places an ash pile on the calling reference; an optional integer selects the pile type.
notes: Optional iType: 1 is the normal ash pile, 2 is the plasma goo pile; omitting it attaches the default.

functions.summary: Enables (1) or disables (0) automatic on-screen display of the active quest's objectives, used when the Pip-Boy cannot be opened.
Forces an autosave into the current autosave slot.
Console command that executes a list of console commands read from a text file in the game folder.
Console command that finds the shortest route between the player and the calling reference, printing it and drawing it as a ground line.
notes: First parameter ignoreLocks is 0 or 1; the other two parameters are unused.

functions.summary: Unused leftover from Oblivion that takes an effect and optional target but does nothing when executed.
notes: Scripts still compile with it but nothing happens; the immediate-cast functions are the replacements.

functions.summary: Makes the calling actor apply a self-targeted actor effect or ingestible to itself instantly, skipping the casting animation.
notes: Only works with effects whose range includes Self.
Effects need a duration above zero; zero duration, even with the no-duration flag, prevents activation. A very long duration can substitute.
An ingestible's form can be given in place of the effect.
Unlike AddSpell, affects only the reference rather than the base object, and the effect has a duration.

functions.summary: Console command that moves the player to a named interior cell.
notes: The player is placed at the cell's COC marker heading; without one placement may be bad, such as inside a wall.

functions.summary: Console command that moves the player to given exterior grid coordinates in the current worldspace.
Console command that moves the player to given exterior grid coordinates in a chosen worldspace.
Condition function returning true when the given challenge has its start-disabled flag set.
Clears the player-enemy crime flag on every crime-tracking faction of the given actor.
Resets all destruction state on the calling reference, including health, model swap, damage stages and self damage, to defaults.
Resets the player-enemy flag on a crime-tracking faction, which is set after the player commits a serious crime against it.
Console debugging command that removes location markers placed in the current cell, paired with PlaceLocationMarker.
Restores the no-activation sound to its default.
Removes the owner from the calling reference.
notes: Clearing does not make the player the owner, which can cause side effects such as teleport doors appearing red; SetOwnership is the alternative.

functions.summary: Console-oriented command that clears blood overlaying the screen after the player took damage.
Clears the screen splatter effect.
Console-only command that closes every open menu; it cannot be used from scripts.
Console command that clears the console's displayed output.
Marks every objective of the given quest as completed.
Console-only command marking all stages of all quests as completed.
Marks the quest completed, dimming it, moving it below active quests in the Pip-Boy, making it unselectable as active, and showing the quest-completed message.
Returns the cosine of an angle in degrees, or with the optional arc flag set returns the arccosine in degrees.
notes: Optional second integer parameter: nonzero switches to the inverse (arccosine) result in degrees.

functions.summary: Generates a detection (noise) event at the calling location reference, owned by an actor, which nearby actors may investigate.
notes: Parameters: owner actor reference, sound level, and optional event type.
Vanilla loud events cap at 100 but any positive sound level is accepted.
Optional event type codes: bullet 0, beam 1, explosion 2, generic 3.

functions.summary: Lowers the damage modifier of an actor value on the calling actor by the given amount, reducing its current value.
notes: The damage modifier is always zero or negative, so the current value drops by the given amount; accepts floats.
Changes are not permanent in the way ModActorValue changes are; RestoreActorValue reverses damage.
Does not work on non-actors; DamageObject is for those.

functions.summary: Applies a float amount of damage to a destructible, not-yet-destroyed object reference.
notes: Does not work on objects with their own health such as weapons, nor on actors.

functions.summary: Console-only command that turns off all VATS body-part highlights.
Console command that unloads a menu from memory by its menu class name.
Console-only debugging command that immediately removes a reference and releases its memory.
notes: Deletion is baked into the save, but the memory release lasts for the session, so reloading an earlier save in the same session leaves it gone.
Outside debugging, MarkForDelete should be used or the game may crash.

functions.summary: Console command reporting menu stack depth for the top menu and the cursor.
Detonates all C4 placed by the calling actor.
Disables the calling reference, so it is not rendered and disabled actors stop AI processing; takes an optional fade-out flag defaulting to 0.
notes: Scripts on disabled non-actor references still run; scripts on disabled actors keep running until the area is left and then stop, so check GetDisabled.
Disabling a reference that has an enable parent has no effect; the fade-out does not apply to children of an enable parent.
Does not remove the reference from the game or reduce save size; MarkForDelete does that.
No effect on inventory references, and disabled actors cannot be made to activate objects.
Disabling the target of a spell during its script-effect start block makes later spell blocks unpredictable.
bugs: Disabling an object inside the add-event block does not work; the activation block works instead.
Disabling a spell's target in the effect start block makes update blocks fire several times for less than the full duration and the finish block sometimes never runs.

functions.summary: Disables all actors; needs a calling reference and may only take effect on already-loaded actors after a cell change.
Disables every mine in the cell the player currently occupies.
notes: To disable one specific mine reference, activating it works.

functions.summary: Sets the flag recording that the player has ever turned off Hardcore mode, which permanently blocks the Hardcore achievement for that playthrough.
Disables the given navmesh.
notes: Works only with raw form IDs, since navmeshes are not references and load-order index fixups do not apply in compiled scripts.

functions.summary: Disables chosen groups of player controls via seven optional 0/1 flags (movement, Pip-Boy, fighting, point of view, looking, rollover text, sneaking).
notes: With no parameters it disables movement, Pip-Boy, fighting and view toggling, while looking, rollover text and sneaking stay enabled.
Movement flag also blocks activating world objects and partly disables the HUD (action points, health, crosshair).
Pip-Boy flag also disables the wait menu; fighting flag holsters a drawn weapon; POV flag forces first person; sneaking flag forces the player out of sneak.
Looking flag locks the camera; rollover flag hides rollover text on world objects.
Resets image space adapters as a side effect.

functions.summary: Removes a specified actor effect currently affecting the calling actor.
notes: Dispelling the spell whose own script is executing acts like a return, ending the script at that point.
Used that way in an effect-update block placed before the finish block, the finish block never runs and the effect lasts its full duration.

functions.summary: Removes all magic effects currently on the calling actor.
Debug console function making the actor's root node half transparent when any argument is nonzero.
Makes the calling actor drop a given count of an item at its feet.
notes: The function does not hand back a usable reference to the dropped item.
Apparently does not trigger the drop event block when called on the player.
Dropped item stats such as charges and script variables reset as if new.
When dropping part of a stack, which instances (by condition) are dropped is unclear.

functions.summary: Drops the calling item out of the container it sits in; has no effect if it is not in a container.
notes: Acts as a return: lines after it do not execute, since the item destroys itself while leaving inventory.
Unlike RemoveMe, does not keep health, charges or script variables.
Does not trigger the item's drop block.
Dropped item appears beside the container or owner; an item with no model stops running scripts but stays, bloating saves.

functions.summary: Console command writing the model map to a dump file whose name includes an optional suffix argument.
Copies all items from the calling actor or container into a target container.
notes: Scripted duplicates get their script variables zeroed and a new form ID, so checks against the original form fail and scripts referencing it break.
The default game does not use it.
bugs: Fallout 3 version creates new unsaved base objects for scripted items, so duplicated scripted items disappear after reloading a save (FO3).

functions.summary: Copies another actor's stats, including class and level, onto the calling actor reference, with skills and attributes recalculated.
notes: The target actor must have its auto-calculate stats flag set.

functions.summary: Enables a previously disabled reference so it renders and actors resume AI; optional fade-in flag defaults to 1.
notes: Calling it on a reference that has an enable parent has no effect.
On an enable parent the fade-in argument is not forwarded; children are enabled with the default fade-in unless set to pop in individually.

functions.summary: Allows or forbids player fast travel, with optional flags for waiting and for keeping the setting across cell changes.
notes: Arguments: canFastTravel, canWait, keepOnCellChange; wait is forced on whenever fast travel is set to 1.
If keepOnCellChange is not 1, entering an interior and returning to an exterior restores fast travel to enabled.
Setting 1 only permits travel if normal conditions allow, e.g. not over-encumbered or in certain interiors.
Calling with 0 0 1 then 0 0 0 leaves the keep behavior in place, since the second call is effectively ignored.
canWait and keepOnCellChange exist only in New Vegas; Fallout 3 takes one flag (FO3).

functions.summary: Forces a generic loading screen, not location-specific, to appear for a few seconds.
Enables the given navmesh.
notes: Works only with raw form IDs, since navmeshes are not references and load-order index fixups do not apply in compiled scripts.

functions.summary: Re-enables player controls turned off by DisablePlayerControls using seven optional 0/1 flags; with no parameters everything is enabled.
notes: Flag meanings are the same as in DisablePlayerControls.

functions.summary: Forces a trigger-enter event on the calling trigger reference, with the argument naming the reference that entered.
Forces the calling actor to equip an item, with optional flags to prevent unequipping and to hide the equip message.
notes: NoUnequipFlag 1 stops the actor unequipping the item until UnequipItem is used; a slot holding such an item blocks further equips there.
Ingestibles can be passed so the actor consumes them normally, including skill scaling and addiction chance.
Does not run the item's equip block; EquipItemAlt is the variant that does.
With several copies, the lowest-condition one is equipped, unless called the same frame as an add, then the last added is used.
Equipping armor on an NPC does not automatically unequip the item it replaces, unlike for the player.
May fail on items added just before; a delay of several frames after adding helps.
bugs: Equipping a playable item with NoUnequipFlag on an NPC, or a playable non-quest item on the player, then calling RemoveAllItems crashes the game.

functions.summary: Forces a game reload as on player death, showing a given message first and then the reload menu.
bugs: Does not display the chosen message and shows a blank one instead.

functions.summary: Forces the calling actor to re-evaluate its list of AI packages.
notes: Even a must-complete or must-reach-location package is dropped and the list re-evaluated.
Does not touch other AI behavior such as combat or pathing; ResetAI resets everything.
Can be slow with long package lists, so use sparingly.
Calling it while the actor is already updating AI, e.g. right after removing a script package or forcing a flee, may crash.

functions.summary: Tests actor and activator references to check they can be condition-tested; apparently forces spell or effect conditions to be re-evaluated in that frame.
notes: Exact effect is unclear on the page; the page assumes it re-checks effect conditions.

functions.summary: Condition function returning 1 when the self and target references in the condition differ, else 0; used in combat dialogue to detect a distinct second speaker.
notes: In combat dialogue the target is a nearby group member, or the speaker itself when none is near.
The function parameter should be left as the target placeholder.
Used on self in dialogue conditions so a response only plays when another group member is available.

functions.summary: Plays the credits and returns to the main menu.
Fades out all sound except music over the given number of seconds, useful around video playback.
notes: The float is the fade duration in seconds.
Sound seems to come back only after a video plays and ends; otherwise it appears irreversible.

functions.summary: Fires a projectile of the given weapon from the calling reference, which need not be an actor.
notes: Projectile spawns at the reference's center heading straight out, unless the model has a projectile node, in which case it exits there.
On the player, one shot of the equipped weapon's ammo is consumed and the equipped weapon's spread is used.
Enchantments and on-hit script blocks of the fired weapon do not take effect.
bugs: When the player fires a grenade-class weapon whose ammo use is 1, the held weapon model disappears until it is re-equipped.

functions.summary: Flushes non-persistent actors from memory.
bugs: Leaks memory, so it is best avoided.

functions.summary: Makes the given quest the player's active quest.
Sets the actor's current value of a stat to a target by adjusting the modifier, rather than changing the base value like SetActorValue.
notes: Equivalent to a modify call by the difference between the target and the current value, which includes effects and damage, so results vary over time.
Like ModActorValue, the change from a script is permanent; UnforceAV undoes it.
Should not be used on the player since combining with other adjustments can leave the stat permanently wrong.

functions.summary: Makes the calling actor assess threats and flee if one is found, optionally toward a cell or reference.
notes: With no arguments the actor picks where to flee and when to stop; with no threat it stands briefly then resumes its package.
Given a cell, it flees until it reaches that cell.
Given a reference, it flees until reaching it; the cell is then ignored but a valid cell is still needed to compile.
Calling with no arguments on an actor in conversation ends the conversation immediately.

functions.summary: Console-oriented command forcing a combat group strategy (fallback, advance, flank or ambush) on an actor in combat with allies; an empty string clears it.
Forces a radio update.
Writes a fresh save into a new slot, just like a manual player save.
notes: Has the usual save limitations, e.g. fails while a message box is shown.

functions.summary: Unused in New Vegas; makes an actor retreat from a target actor for a set number of seconds.
When run from a terminal menu item's result script, moves the terminal back one level, or closes it from the top level.
Immediately switches weather to the given weather, skipping the normal transition, with an optional flag to hold it until released.
notes: If the override flag is 1, weather stays until ReleaseWeatherOverride is called; otherwise weather returns to normal progression.

functions.summary: Modifies the calling actor's disposition so it reaches friend level with the player.
Console command that prints which menu is topmost.
Returns the reference that most recently interacted with the calling scripted object (activator or trigger).
notes: Only valid during the frame after the interaction, so useful inside activation or trigger enter/leave/stay blocks.
With several interacting objects, only the latest is returned.
Comparing the result to a reference is equivalent to IsActionRef.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the calling actor is the player's enemy because of crimes against that actor itself.
notes: Always 0 if the player has committed no crimes against this actor, even if its factions treat the player as an enemy (see GetActorFactionPlayerEnemy).

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the player is flagged as an enemy, due to crime, of any faction the calling actor belongs to, else 0.
Returns the count of actors currently at the high AI/script processing level, such as those in the loaded interior or the loaded exterior cells around the player.
Returns the current, modified value of an actor value on the calling actor, covering any stat available to actors and the player.
Console command, not for scripts, that prints a detailed breakdown of one actor value on the calling actor.
Returns 1 if the calling actor is alarmed.
Unused function returning the total value of stolen goods the player has sold, counted as money actually received rather than base value.
Returns the calling object's rotation in degrees about the chosen axis (X, Y or Z) relative to the world.
notes: On the player, X ranges about -89 to 89, negative when looking up and positive when looking down.
On the player, Z is a heading from 0 to 360, 0 along the positive Y axis, increasing clockwise.
Z matches compass north only in the Wasteland worldspace; interiors use the coordinate system while the compass uses a cell north marker.
Values are bearings, clockwise from north, not counterclockwise trigonometric angles; a conversion is needed for trigonometry.

functions.summary: Returns an index for the special animation action the calling actor is performing, or -1 if none; works as a script function and condition.
notes: The page gives separate index tables for Fallout 3 and New Vegas; they differ from index 6 on, e.g. reload is 8 in FO3 and 9 in New Vegas.
In New Vegas, 2 is full-auto fire or a melee swing, 3 semi-auto fire, 5 winding up a throw, and 13 covers most other scripted or forced animations.
Not every value is understood; some of 10 to 12 may be leftovers.

functions.summary: Returns the total damage resistance of armor the calling actor currently has equipped.
Returns the weight class of the calling actor's equipped upper-body armor: 0 none, 1 light, 2 medium or heavy.
Gives 1 once the calling actor has been attacked; the state resets when it leaves combat.
bugs: Using it on the player may crash the game.

functions.summary: Returns the base value of a stat for the calling actor.
Returns 1 when the calling radio station broadcasts nonstop, 0 when that is off and it only plays static.
Returns the zero-based index of the message box button just chosen after a ShowMessage call, otherwise -1.
notes: Reports the choice only once after the press; subsequent calls give -1, so store the result in a variable.
Only reacts to a ShowMessage made from the same script.
Works in quest scripts if the script processing delay is 0.1 or lower.
Index follows the button's position in the message definition even when conditional buttons are hidden.
bugs: Calling it in successive if conditions fails for all but the first, because the first call consumes the stored result.

functions.summary: Returns 1 while the calling actor is in the cannibalism animation.
Returns the player's winnings level, 0 to 4, for the given casino form; script-function form used in casino scripts for the achievement and ban dialogue.
notes: GetCasinoWinningStage is the equivalent condition-function form.

functions.summary: Condition-function form returning the player's winnings level, 0 to 4, for the given casino form, used in casino NPC dialogue.
Returns an integer code for how the calling actor died.
notes: The page lists codes: -1 none, 0 explosion, 2 gun, 3 blunt weapon, 4 hand to hand, 5 object impact, 6 poison, 7 radiation.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the given challenge has been completed; a recurring challenge counts once completed at least once.
Returns the clothing value, from 0 to 100 as a float, of the armor the calling actor is wearing.
Returns a reference to whomever the calling actor is currently fighting.
notes: Works on the player, giving whichever actor is being aimed at when within auto-aim range.
Yields a value right after the player's thrown or fired explosive or melee attack strikes an actor, or when auto-aim locks on.
Seems to use the same data that drives the HUD target health bar.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the calling actor is concussed.
Returns a reference to the container holding the calling object, if any.
Returns how many items the calling container holds in total, useful for emptiness checks.
Returns an integer identifying the AI package type the calling actor is currently running.
notes: The page lists codes 0 to 37 (explore, follow, combat, dialogue, wander, travel, sandbox, patrol and others); not all numbers are used.

functions.summary: Returns an integer identifying the AI procedure the calling actor is currently performing.
notes: The page lists codes 0 to 50 for procedures such as travel, wait, combat, flee and sandbox.
Procedure differs from package; one package can pass through several procedures, and procedures can switch without any package change.

functions.summary: Returns the current game time of day as a decimal float in hours, e.g. 4.5 for 4:30 am and 19.75 for 7:45 pm.
Returns a float from 0.0 to 1.0 for how far the weather transition has progressed; a value strictly between means a transition is under way.
Gives the weekday as an integer, Sunday being 0 and Saturday 6.
Returns 1 if the calling actor reference is dead, else 0.
notes: More reliable than checking health, since an actor can die without losing all health, e.g. via KillActor.
Not 1 for an actor disabled while alive, but stays 1 if deleted or disabled after death.
An essential actor reduced to zero health and made unconscious is not dead; KnockedState checks that.

functions.summary: Returns the total number of actors of the given base actor type that have been killed.
notes: Because it takes a base actor ID, it cannot tell whether one specific named reference died.
On a templated actor it counts only the specified reference.
Resurrecting an actor does not reduce the count.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the calling object's default state is open.
Returns 1 if the calling reference is destroyed, else 0.
Returns the current damage stage of the calling reference, or -1 if it has no destruction data or has taken no object health damage.
Returns 1 if the calling actor currently detects the target reference, usable as script or condition function.
notes: Can remain true for a dead actor, since the detection value is not updated after death until the area reloads.
After a fire event with a hidden caller, detection may lag a few frames, so check later with a delayed call.

functions.summary: Returns the calling actor's detection level of a target actor, 0 to 3: lost, unseen, noticed, seen.
notes: Usable as script or condition function.
bugs: In testing it returns only 0 when the target is the player, and only 0 or 3 for other targets.

functions.summary: Gives an integer from 0 to 7 naming the emotion an actor currently shows during dialogue.
notes: Codes listed: neutral 0, anger 1, disgust 2, fear 3, sad 4, happy 5, surprise 6, pained 7.

functions.summary: Unused function meant to return the intensity of an actor's dialogue emotion as a float.
bugs: Does not work and always returns 0.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the calling reference is disabled, else 0.
Returns the calling actor's current disposition toward a target actor, including all active modifiers.
Returns the distance in game units, as a float, between the calling reference and a target reference.
bugs: Passing a null reference, or one outside the current cell, crashes the script.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the calling actor has the given object equipped.
notes: Only checks armor and weapon objects; armor addons such as built-in gloves or weapon parts are not detected.
A form list may be passed; true if any listed item is equipped by the character.

functions.summary: Returns the combat reaction between two factions as an integer.
notes: Codes: 0 neutral (default for unspecified pairs), 1 enemy, 2 ally, 3 friend.
Very aggressive actors attack neutral factions; enemy factions get attacked immediately by aggressive and very aggressive actors.
Allies and friends never attack each other; the assistance setting decides whether they help each other.

functions.summary: Gives the calling actor's rank within a faction, -1 when it is not a member.
Returns the rank difference in a given faction between the calling actor and a target actor.
Gives a float disposition modifier that applies between two factions.
Returns the faction relation between the calling actor and another actor as an integer: 0 neutral, 1 enemy, 2 ally, 3 friend.
Returns the calling actor's current fatigue actor value divided by its base fatigue, as a float.
Condition function giving 1 when the actor is flagged to play a forced hit reaction, otherwise 0.
notes: The base game hardcodes it to 1 after certain power attacks (two custom power attacks and the uppercut), used to select idles normally for crippled limbs.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the calling actor is currently in a forced-run state.
Returns 1 if the calling actor is currently in a forced-sneak state.
Returns how many friendly hits the target actor has made on the calling actor.
notes: Typically used in dialogue conditions to detect the player attacking a friend and trigger a warning.

functions.summary: Returns the type of furniture the calling actor is currently using: 0 none, 1 to 10 beds, 11 to 20 chairs; the idle manager uses it to pick animations.
Returns the current value of the named game setting.
Gives the current value stored in a global variable.
notes: Mainly useful in dialogue conditions, since scripts can read a global directly by name.
In scripts it accepts a variable name directly, effectively a typed-in form ID, but not string variables, only reference variables.

functions.summary: Unused function that would return the player's gold amount; checking the item count of the caps item is the alternative.
Returns how many members are in the calling actor's combat group; 0 if not an actor or not in combat, 1 if fighting alone.
Returns how many targets are in the calling actor's combat group; yields 0 for non-actors, actors not in combat, or groups with no targets.
Tests whether the player's Pip-Boy holds a given note, giving 1 if so and 0 otherwise; no calling reference, with the note form as the sole argument.
Returns, as a float from -180 to 180, the angle between the calling reference's facing and the given object; returns 0 if the caller is not an actor.
notes: The caller's facing direction counts as zero; clockwise offsets are positive, counter-clockwise ones negative.
Differs from the world-relative Z angle getter; adding the result to the caller's current Z angle makes it face the target.

functions.summary: Returns an actor's current health as a fraction of its base health, as a float where 1.0 means full health.
notes: Health-increasing base effects can push the result above 1.
Computed as current Health actor value divided by base Health; if the base value is zero, the result is 1.0.

functions.summary: Returns an integer index for the body location struck by an actor's most recent hit, with -1 meaning none.
notes: Page lists the index table: -1 none, 0 torso, 1-2 heads, 3-6 arms, 7-12 legs, 13 brain, 14 hand or weapon.
Always -1 when the hit came from an explosion.
A typical human actor only uses locations 0, 1, 3, 5, 7 and 10, as set by the default body part data.
Inside a GameMode block it is only correct on the frame the reference dies.
bugs: Value is not available inside OnHit and OnHitWith blocks.
Fails inside a weapon's object effect, though the weapon's critical effect can use it.

functions.summary: Reports 1 when the actor is set to disregard crimes, and 0 when it reports crimes by the player (the default).
notes: Flag values: 0 reports crimes, 1 does not report them.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the actor is set to ignore friendly hits, else 0.
Returns 1 if the actor's current cell name begins with the given cell name, else 0.
notes: Only interior cell names are accepted as the argument; exterior cells do not work.
To cover related interior and exterior cells under one prefix, a dummy interior cell with that name may be needed.

functions.summary: Like GetInCell but not called on a reference: returns 1 if the actor passed as the second argument is in a cell matching the given cell name.
notes: Only interior cell names are accepted as the cell argument; exteriors do not work.
Matching is by name prefix, so one name can cover many related interior cells.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the character-generation state has been set (via the matching setter), else 0.
notes: Not usable as a condition on actor effects.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the calling actor belongs to the given faction, else 0.
notes: When used as a dialogue condition, it overrides the Allow Default Dialogue flag restriction.

functions.summary: Outputs the current value of an INI setting given as setting name and section; console-only, with no return value.
bugs: Does not work correctly for some renderer-related INI settings, such as the full-screen flag.

functions.summary: Returns 1 when the calling reference and the target actor occupy one cell, else 0.
notes: In exteriors it returns false for adjacent actors separated by a cell boundary, so a grid-based check is better.
Passing an NPC or creature base form is accepted but makes the script fail; use a reference.

functions.summary: Returns 1 when the calling actor stands in an exterior cell of the given worldspace; always 0 inside interiors.
Returns 1 if the calling reference is in a cell attached to the given encounter zone, else 0.
Returns 1 when the actor is in its alerted state; that state only drives animation and leaves real combat status untouched.
Returns 1 if the calling actor has the given alignment, else 0.
notes: Valid alignment names: VeryGood, Good, Neutral, Evil, VeryEvil.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the calling actor's class is the given class form.
Returns 1 if the calling actor is a creature, meaning form type 43.
Returns 1 if the calling creature is of the creature type given by integer parameter.
notes: Page includes a creature type table mapping numbers to types.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the calling actor is currently running the given AI package, else 0.
Returns 1 if the given weather form is the currently active weather, else 0.
Returns 1 if the calling object has the given form type, passed as its four-character signature (e.g. ACTI, CONT, CREA).
Returns 1 if the calling actor reference is flagged as a ghost, else 0.
notes: The ghost state's effects are described under the setter for it.

functions.summary: Returns 1 when the caller is a placed instance of the given base object, else 0.
notes: Cannot test the player by editor ID; compare against the player's form ID (7) instead.

functions.summary: Returns 1 when the caller's lock has been broken, else 0.
notes: A perk entry point making the player ignore broken locks (nonzero) grants a second lockpick chance after the first break, so the result stays 0 then.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the calling object is of the given form type, passed as the full type name (e.g. Activator, Container).
Returns 1 if the calling NPC's race is a playable race, 0 for races such as ghouls or raider-specific races; takes no parameter.
Returns 1 if the calling actor's race is the given race form.
Returns 1 when the calling object is exactly the reference passed in, unlike GetIsID, which compares base objects.
notes: The reference passed must be persistent.

functions.summary: Returns 1 when the calling actor's sex matches the argument, Male or Female.
Returns 1 if the actor is using the given item form, else 0.
Returns 1 if the item currently being used or activated has the given equip type, else 0.
Returns 1 if the item currently being used or activated has the given form type, else 0.
notes: Argument must be the form type's full name, not its numeric ID.

functions.summary: Returns 1 when the calling actor uses the given voice type.
Returns how many of the given item the calling container, actor or creature holds.
notes: The item may be a reference variable.
If a form list is passed, the result is the sum of counts across the listed items.
Does not work for notes; the note-specific check should be used instead.
bugs: Sometimes returns a nonzero count for items not really present when they came from leveled lists.

functions.summary: Returns an integer naming the limb struck last (dismembered, exploded or still whole) at the moment the calling actor died.
notes: Page lists the limb index table: -1 none, 0 torso, 1-2 heads, 3-6 arms, 7-12 legs, 13 brain, 14 hand or weapon.

functions.summary: Returns the calling actor's knocked state as an integer.
notes: Values: -1 fatigue knockout, 0 normal, 1 knocked out (incl. unconscious essential, paralyzed, negative-fatigue), 2 knocked down.
Returns 0 for actors knocked down by the push-away command.
bugs: An essential actor knocked out before recovering from a push-away still reports 0, as though the push were ongoing.

functions.summary: Returns whether the actor's most recent hit was a critical; the data can be read inside on-hit script blocks.
notes: Readable from OnHit and OnHitWith blocks.
Offered in the condition menu, but whether it works correctly as a condition is unclear.

functions.summary: Returns the index of the player's most recent action; the page includes an action index table.
Returns the current level of the calling actor as an integer.
Returns true when the calling actor can see the given object; only valid on actors.
notes: On a non-player actor, the target must itself be an actor or the result is false even when visible.
On the player, any object may be tested, but non-actor targets are slow; and the test uses the camera's view, not the character's.
Field of view is about 95 degrees either side of straight ahead, identical for every non-player actor regardless of eye placement.
Trigger and collision volumes in view count as visible; disabled references never do.
bugs: Calling it on a disabled actor, or one disabled the previous frame, can crash; a short delay after enabling avoids it.

functions.summary: Returns the reference linked to the calling reference (for example a switch's linked door); takes no parameters.
Returns the access state of a door, container or terminal as an integer.
notes: Doors and containers: 0 unlocked or not locked, 1 locked but openable with key or lockpick, 2 locked out (impossible lock level or broken).
Terminals: 0 unlocked (note held, no lock data, or script-unlocked), 1 has lock data, 2 locked out (failed hack or impossible level).
bugs: Hacking a terminal does not change its state; any terminal that is or was locked reports 1 unless a script unlocks it.

functions.summary: Gives the lock difficulty of a terminal, or of a door or container lock, as an integer.
notes: Lock values: 0, 25, 50, 75, 100 for very easy to very hard, and 255 impossible.
Terminal values: 0 to 4 for very easy to very hard, and 5 impossible.
Describes pick or hack difficulty only, not access state; leveled locks and terminals return their leveled value.

functions.summary: Gives the count of serious offences the player has racked up against the calling NPC.
Returns how visible the calling map marker is, as an integer.
notes: Values: 0 not visible on map, 1 visible but not fast-travel enabled, 2 visible and fast-travel enabled.

functions.summary: Gives the count of petty offences the player has racked up against the calling NPC.
Returns 1 if the given quest objective index is marked completed, else 0; takes quest and objective index.
Returns 1 if the given quest objective index is currently displayed, else 0; takes quest and objective index.
notes: Stays 1 while shown in the Pip-Boy even if the objective or quest is completed; combine with the completed check to test active ones.

functions.summary: Returns true when the calling actor's present package lets it offer services.
notes: Returns false while the NPC is in conversation with another NPC or moving to a destination.
Setting up a travel package mid-journey, even one offering services, leaves the NPC temporarily non-offering while it walks.
bugs: As a vendor dialogue condition it may crash New Vegas when a further vendor is set up via a talking activator.

functions.summary: Returns an animating door's open state as an integer; also valid for some objects with open and closed animations.
notes: Values: none 0, open 1, opening 2, closed 3, closing 4.
Also meaningful for some radios and containers.
These values do not match those used by the matching setter.

functions.summary: Gives the most recent target of whoever owns the calling reference; may be called on a form.
Returns the reference that is the calling actor's current AI package target, if any.
notes: For an actor in conversation, returns the conversation partner.

functions.summary: Returns the enable parent reference set in the reference dialog; a reference follows its parent's enable and disable state.
Tells whether the player counts as an enemy of the faction passed.
Returns 1 when the player has been expelled from the faction passed.
Returns 1 if the player is a member of the given faction, else 0.
Returns 1 if the player's class matches the given class form.
Returns 1 if the player's race matches the given race; the player-only version of GetIsRace.
Tests the player's gender against Male or Female and returns 1 on a match, else 0.
Returns the value of a named player miscellaneous statistic, given as a string.
notes: Page lists the valid stat names separately for Fallout 3 and New Vegas, with New Vegas adding many (e.g. gambling and crafting stats).

functions.summary: Gives the hours of sleep the player picked in the menu, or 0 when the player is awake.
Returns an actor value's permanent value, like the base value but also including permanent modifiers such as skill books.
notes: Excludes temporary bonuses from perks with entry points, equipped items and drugs.
The Tag! perk is reflected only because it permanently modifies the skill through its own function.

functions.summary: Tells whether an armed explosive is attached to the calling actor.
Returns 1 if any of the selected player controls are disabled, else 0; each optional flag picks a control group.
notes: Optional flags: movement, Pip-Boy, fighting, point of view, looking, rollover text, sneaking.
With no arguments it behaves as if every flag were set.
Result is true when any one of the selected controls is disabled.

functions.summary: Returns the reference of the object held by the player's grab at the moment, or none.
Opens the player's name entry menu; despite the name it does not return the player's name.
notes: Same behaviour as the show-name-menu function.

functions.summary: Returns 1 when the calling actor has been made a teammate of the player.
Returns how many actors are currently set as player teammates.
Returns the calling object's world position on the given axis (X, Y or Z) as a float.
Returns 1 if the quest was marked complete or failed, else 0; the quest argument is optional.
notes: Does not need the quest to be running; stays true after the quest is stopped if it was also marked complete.
True for failed quests too; a separate failed check tells the two apart.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the named quest is currently running, else 0.
Returns the value of a named variable in a quest's script; takes quest and variable name.
notes: Condition function only; scripts read quest variables with dotted quest.variable syntax.

functions.summary: Returns the radiation level of the calling actor's current surroundings as a float.
notes: Proportional to the rads-per-second meter: level 3 gives 3 rads per second.
An actor's own accumulated radiation is a separate actor value.

functions.summary: Returns a random integer from 0 to 99 inclusive.
Returns the player's fame or infamy with a reputation faction; the second argument selects infamy (0) or fame (1).
bugs: Does not reliably return a value unless used inside a conditional expression.

functions.summary: Returns the player's fame or infamy with a reputation as a 0 to 1 fraction of that reputation's maximum; second argument 0 is infamy, 1 fame.
notes: Equals the raw fame or infamy value divided by the reputation's scale.

functions.summary: Returns the player's reputation tier (0 to 6) with a reputation, given an axis argument: 0 mixed, 1 good, 2 bad.
notes: Only one axis is nonzero at a time; with zero fame and infamy, all three axes return 1.
Higher fame returns 2 to 6 on the good axis and 0 on the others, and similarly for infamy.
Page lists the tier names per axis, with 0 meaning none of the tiers, 1 neutral.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the actor was set restrained with the matching setter, else 0.
notes: Restrained actors stay in place but still run AI, detection and dialogue.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the calling actor is currently carrying out a Sandman action, the silent sleeping-NPC kill tied to the Mister Sandman perk.
Returns the raw scale of the calling reference as a float, where 1.0 is normal size.
Gives the value of a local variable declared in the given object's script; takes the object and the variable name.
notes: Condition function only; in scripts, read such variables with dotted object.variable syntax.

functions.summary: Returns the real-time seconds elapsed since this same script last called the function, as a float.
notes: Scaled by the global time multiplier; divide by that multiplier for true real-world time.
Each script tracks its last call independently.
Multiple calls in one script within one frame give the same value.
Unreliable in script effects during sleep, wait or fast travel; a dedicated elapsed-seconds function exists for that.

functions.summary: Returns the reference ID of the calling reference, mainly for passing that reference as a parameter; also usable under the alias this.
notes: Returns null with no valid calling reference, or when the caller is a non-persistent item.
Should not be used in scripts on items that can be in inventory.
Returns 0 for dynamically created references, such as those from PlaceAtMe or dropped from inventory.

functions.summary: Returns the calling actor's sitting state as an integer.
notes: Values: 0 not sitting, 1 loading sitting idle, 2 getting ready to sit, 3 sitting, 4 getting ready to stand.

functions.summary: Returns the calling actor's sleeping state as an integer.
notes: Values: 0 not sleeping, 1 loading sleeping idle, 2 getting ready to sleep, 3 sleeping, 4 getting ready to wake.
Does not work on the player; use the player-specific sleeping check.

functions.summary: Returns how many times an actor has used a given ingestible while its effects are active, scaled by effect magnitude; needs a usage monitor effect on the ingestible.
notes: Yields a usage value only during the ingestible's active effect period.
bugs: Does not handle usage monitor effects configured to decrease over time.

functions.summary: Returns the highest completed stage of a quest, regardless of the order stages were completed in.
notes: For checking whether one particular stage was done, the stage-done function is the right one.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the given stage of the given quest has been completed, else 0.
Returns the original rotation of the calling object on the chosen axis (X, Y or Z), as placed in the editor rather than its current angle.
Returns the original position of the calling object on the chosen axis (X, Y or Z), as placed in the editor rather than its current position.
Returns 1 when the calling NPC has at any time conversed with the player, else 0.
Same as GetTalkedToPC but takes the NPC as an argument instead of a calling reference; returns 1 if it has ever spoken to the player.
Returns the computed threat ratio between the calling actor and the actor passed as the argument, as a float.
Returns how many hours the calling actor has been dead, as a float; 0 if invalid, not dead, not loaded or disabled.
notes: Disabling a dead actor discards its death-time info, so it still returns 0 after re-enabling.

functions.summary: Returns how many warnings the calling actor (guard-package, trespass or aggro-radius responder) has given the specified reference.
Returns 1 if the actor was put into an unconscious state through the matching setter, else 0.
notes: Does not detect unconsciousness from fatigue damage or an essential actor losing all health; the knocked-state check covers those.

functions.summary: Returns whether the actor is currently using or activating an item; the page marks this as uncertain.
notes: Only used in the base game as a condition on idle animations.

functions.summary: Unused leftover that checks whether an actor is a vampire; it never returns anything but 0.
notes: Customarily used as an always-false condition to disable content such as topic infos.

functions.summary: Returns the player's current VATS view mode as an integer.
notes: Values: 0 none, 1 target select, 2 menu mode, 3 scan mode, 4 playback.

functions.summary: Gives the Z offset between the player and the center of the targeted limb or bounding volume in VATS, as a float.
Condition function taking a query name and optional parameter that reports VATS attack details, usable only for camera path selection or the to-hit chance entry point.
notes: Gives no meaningful value outside VATS playback or the to-hit entry point.
In the to-hit entry point, outcomes such as success, critical, dismemberment and damage are not yet computed; the weapon, target and aimed limb are already known.
Page lists queries: weapon, weapon-list, weapon-type and target checks, target distance, targeted part, VATS action, success, critical, crit effect, fatal, explode, dismember and cripple.
Most queries return 1 or 0; target distance returns the distance in units.

functions.summary: Returns the calling actor's walk speed as a float.
Returns an integer for the calling actor's current weapon animation type, which the page tabulates.
notes: Distinguishes only 11 animation types plus a catch-all, merging several of the 13 (FO3) or 14 (New Vegas) internal types.
Created for VATS camera conditions.

functions.summary: Returns the condition (health) of the calling actor's equipped weapon as a float percentage of its base condition.
Returns the wind speed of the current weather as a float between 0.0 and 1.0, defined on the weather record.
Returns the amount of experience the player needs to reach the next level.
Returns 1 when the player has eaten the calling actor, possible only with cannibalism; used as a condition in the Cannibal perk.
notes: Usable in scripts, but whether it stays valid long after the actor was consumed is untested.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the calling actor's disposition is at or above the friend disposition game setting, else 0; also a condition function.
Returns 1 when the calling reference has 3D currently loaded.
Returns 1 when the calling reference is under the influence of the given magic base effect.
Returns whether the calling actor has the given perk; an optional flag makes it test the player's teammates instead.
notes: On the player, a nonzero second argument asks about the player's teammates rather than the player.

functions.summary: Console-only command that lists console commands, script functions, game settings and INI settings containing a search word.
Console-only command that draws a flickering VATS-style highlight on the calling reference; persists for the session.
notes: Many references can be highlighted, with a hardcoded cap of 32.
The most recently highlighted one is the one that flashes.

functions.summary: Console-only command that highlights a chosen body part on the calling reference, whether object, item or living actor; persists for the session.
notes: Without an index it highlights everything except the weapon.
A single body part highlight is active at once.

functions.summary: Sets whether the calling NPC ignores crimes, stopping it from attacking or reporting the player for them.
notes: Flag 0 means crimes are reported (default); 1 means they are not.
Non-friend, non-ally actors still react to being attacked directly, but do not report it as a crime.

functions.summary: Advances progress toward the threshold of the given challenge; used by the Dead Money add-on.
Inside an OnActivate block, returns 1 if the given reference was the one that activated the calling object.
notes: Meaningful only inside an OnActivate block.

functions.summary: Returns 1 when the calling reference is a creature or NPC, else 0.
Returns 1 when the caller is the NPC currently designated as crime victim; only one at a time, mostly gating crime dialogue.
Returns 1 when any other actor currently detects the caller, else 0.
notes: Always 0 when called on the player.
Cannot tell whether the player has detected an actor; a line-of-sight check is the alternative for that.

functions.summary: Returns 1 when the caller is in one or more evil factions and in no non-evil ones.
notes: Works only on NPCs; creatures are never considered evil whatever their factions.

functions.summary: Returns 1 or 0 for whether the actor reference is essential; the page is a stub.
Returns 1 when AI has been switched off for the caller, else 0.
Returns true if the actor is speaking via an activator; the actor must first be registered through the talking-activator setter.
notes: As a dialogue condition it must run on the linked reference, with no second parameter.
Practically a condition function, since it is true only during dialogue through the activator.
Also true while the actor sits in a dialogue package, e.g. awaiting a reply in a conversation with another actor.
False if the talking actor was assigned by script.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if hardcore mode has been on throughout the game; used to verify the hardcore achievement requirements.
Returns 1 if the calling object is playing an animation; with an optional animation group it only counts animations of that group's sequence type.
notes: The group-filtered form is less reliable; extended and alternate variants are more dependable.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the named cell is owned by the given NPC or faction; with the second argument omitted it tests for player ownership.
Returns 1 if the calling actor is a child, taken from the child flag of its race.
notes: Unrelated to the player-young setting function.

functions.summary: Reports whether the current weather is cloudy: 0 not cloudy, a fraction between 0 and 1 while transitioning to cloudy, 1 when stable and cloudy.
Returns 1 if the given actor is a combat target of the calling reference, else 0.
Returns 1 if the calling actor wants a new package but is held on its current one because that package continues while the player is near.
notes: Depends on the Continue-if-PC-near flag of the current package and the player being in the same cell.

functions.summary: Returns 1 when the calling NPC is seated on a furniture reference of the given furniture base type.
Returns 1 if the calling NPC is sitting on the specific furniture reference given.
Returns 1 when the caller carries the essential flag, else 0.
Idle-manager check returning 1 when a knocked-down creature lies facing upward.
notes: For quadrupeds, the left-side-up check should be used instead.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if gore is disabled, else 0.
Returns 1 if hardcore mode is currently active, else 0.
Returns 1 if the calling actor is playing a special idle animation, else 0.
Returns 1 if the given image space modifier is currently active, else 0.
notes: Despite its name, it takes a modifier rather than an image space, and cannot be called on image spaces.

functions.summary: Returns 1 when the caller is in combat now, else 0.
notes: Also 1 while enemies are in active search for the player.
If the caller never entered combat but changed cells through a load door with enemies near, it may keep returning 1 for a couple of seconds.

functions.summary: Returns 1 when the reference is at the given critical effect stage.
notes: Valid stages: None, GooStart, GooEnd, DisintegrateStart, DisintegrateEnd.

functions.summary: Returns 1 when the calling actor is standing in damaging water.
Returns 1 when the caller lies in an interior cell, else 0.
Returns 1 if the calling reference's base object is in the given form list, else 0.
notes: Returns 0 if the list holds the reference itself instead of its base form.

functions.summary: Returns 1 when the caller is within a cell it owns.
notes: True if the actor itself or one of its factions owns the cell.

functions.summary: Returns 1 when the given actor killed the calling actor, else 0.
notes: Killer data is lost if the actor has been disabled.

functions.summary: Presumably like IsKiller but for an object that can kill things; the page is uncertain and sparse.
Idle-manager check returning 1 when a knocked-down quadruped has its left flank up.
notes: Bipeds should use the facing-up check instead.

functions.summary: Returns whether the calling actor has a given limb dismembered; a second optional index makes it test any limb across a range.
notes: Limb indices follow the same body location table as the hit-location getter (0 torso through 13 brain).
With two indices, it tests whether any limb from the first to the second is missing.

functions.summary: Returns the direction in which the calling actor is currently requesting to move, as an integer.
notes: Codes: no movement is 0; forward, backward, left and right are 1, 2, 3 and 4 respectively.

functions.summary: Passing 1 hides every menu and the console; the Pip-Boy restores them when opened.
Returns 1 when the given faction or NPC directly owns the calling object, or the player when no argument is passed.
notes: Checks only ownership set on the reference, not ownership inherited from the cell.
Returns 0 when the owner is NONE, so it cannot detect public ownership.

functions.summary: Returns 1 for a first-person camera and 0 for third-person.
bugs: Can return 1 for a single frame in third person when aiming or un-aiming a scoped weapon, opening or closing the Pip-Boy, or entering or leaving VATS.
On scoped-weapon aim frames, the scope-use check returns 0, and for VATS transition frames the VATS mode check returns 0, so those cannot filter the false positives.

functions.summary: Returns 1 once the player has murdered any non-evil NPC.
Returns 1 while the player is asleep in a bed, excluding waiting.
Returns 1 if the player is currently performing the action selected by a numeric action index (values 1 to 10), otherwise 0.
notes: Several actions may be active simultaneously, and each one reports true.
Some actions stay active on a timer, others only while being performed; weapon firing lingers about two game minutes, while standing on furniture clears immediately.
The fire-weapon action turns on when the attack button is pressed, not when the projectile leaves, for every ranged type, even with no ammo.
The page includes an action index table of valid values.
bugs: The iron-sights action (9), and perhaps others, does not report true during combat, probably because the function was meant for dialogue comments.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the player is currently holding (grabbing) the given object reference, otherwise 0.
Yields 1 when the player stands within the named region, otherwise 0; an interior cell always gives 0.
notes: Nested regions both count: a player in a child region also tests true for the parent.

functions.summary: Yields 1 during the transition into a new space (fast travel or load door passage), otherwise 0.
notes: Followers are relocated before the player arrives, so using this as a follow-package condition lets them re-evaluate location conditions during the load.
It reads 1 only while the loading screen is shown, so scripts may only see it inside MenuMode, OnLoad or comparable blocks.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the given skill occupies any of the player's tag skill slots, otherwise 0.
Returns 0 if current weather is not pleasant, a fraction between 0 and 1 while transitioning to pleasant weather, and 1 when pleasant weather is stable.
Yields 1 when the game runs on a PlayStation 3, otherwise 0.
notes: On the PC game this always yields false, since a PS3 controller cannot be correctly detected.

functions.summary: Yields 1 when the current weather is settled rain, otherwise 0.
notes: Unlike the Oblivion version, it only ever returns 0 or 1, so rain transitions must be detected by combining it with the current weather percent (FO3).

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the calling actor's movement speed mode is currently set to run rather than walk.
notes: Actors have only walk and run speeds; run is the default player pace unless toggle walk is used.
It reports the selected speed mode even when the actor is standing still, so pair it with IsMoving to detect real running.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the calling actor is sneaking (crouched), otherwise 0.
Yields 1 when the current weather is settled snow, otherwise 0.
notes: Unlike the Oblivion version, it only ever returns 0 or 1, so snow transitions must be detected by combining it with the current weather percent (FO3).

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the calling actor is currently affected by the given magic item (spell, enchantment or ingestible such as food, drink or chem).
notes: Passing an addiction effect returns 1 whenever the actor is addicted, even when not currently in withdrawal.
Passing a chem item itself can show whether the actor is currently under its influence, which helps tell if an addiction was just satisfied.
bugs: The page marks this function as deprecated and unreliable; the alternative versions that list active effects are recommended instead.

functions.summary: Yields 1 when the calling actor is swimming, otherwise 0.
notes: The Z coordinate can substitute in the Wasteland worldspace, but only for the main auto-generated water body, not placed water.
bugs: Always returns 0 when called on the player.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the calling actor is currently speaking, otherwise 0.
Called on a talking activator reference with an actor argument; returns 1 if that actor is the one currently speaking through the activator.
notes: Returns false when the activator's actor was assigned through a script.

functions.summary: Returns 1 while time is passing in menu mode because the player is sleeping, waiting or travelling, otherwise 0.
Returns 1 if the actor currently has a torch out; an unused leftover from Oblivion.
Returns 1 if the calling actor is currently trespassing, otherwise 0.
Reports whether the calling actor is turning, using a three-valued result: none, left or right.
notes: Results are 0 for no turn, 1 for a left turn and 2 for a right turn.

functions.summary: Yields 1 when the calling actor is in the waiting state set by the wait function, otherwise 0.
Yields 1 when whatever is being activated is placeable water; the base game uses it for the drinking animation.
Returns 1 if the weapon the calling actor currently has equipped is a member of the given form list, otherwise 0.
Yields 1 when the calling actor has a weapon drawn, otherwise 0.
notes: The value flips when the weapon attaches to the weapon node; for NPCs this is the end of the equip or unequip animation.
Creatures without a weapon always return 0.
It turns 1 only about midway through the equip animation; checking the animation action for -1 reveals when the animation is over.

functions.summary: Yields 1 when the calling reference is a weapon that uses the given skill, otherwise 0.
notes: Available only as a condition, not in scripts; the weapon-skill getter is the scripting alternative (FO3).

functions.summary: Yields 1 when the game runs on a PC, otherwise 0.
Yields 1 when the game runs on the Xbox, otherwise 0.
notes: On PC it also returns true when an Xbox controller (or Steam controller) is used, so it is unsuitable for blocking content from players.
bugs: Reports true on PC whenever an Xbox-style controller is in use.

functions.summary: Kills the calling actor, with optional arguments naming the killer, which body part to dismember, and how death is categorised.
notes: Dismembering a part also dismembers every severable or explodable part sharing its actor value; non-explodable parts will not explode.
Can be used on already dead actors to dismember limbs; the page lists numeric limb locations 0 to 14.
Essential actors only fall unconscious for a few seconds; scaled-down (child-sized) actors may be immune.
If the actor is outside the player's cell, all their items get unequipped.
Destruction data effects such as turret death explosions are not triggered. Passing the player as killer shows limb crippled messages.

functions.summary: Kills every actor in the loaded area: the grid of cells around the player in an exterior, or the player's current cell in an interior; optional killer argument.
notes: Essential actors are put into their usual temporary unconscious state rather than being killed.

functions.summary: Loads the named savegame if it exists; an optional integer of 1 writes debug information about the save to a text file.
Locks the calling terminal, container or door, optionally setting a new lock level via the integer argument.
notes: Level 0 (the default) locks without altering the existing level, so the very-easy level cannot be set this way; 1 to 255 sets the level and locks.
Lock level codes differ between doors/containers (0 to 255 scale) and terminals (0 to 5 scale); page lists both tables.
It overrides any previous lock level including unlocked, and overrides an earlier Unlock call.
It cannot revoke terminal access gained through a password note or a successful hack, and a failed hack stays locked out; only the level changes.
The given level is a base value; a leveled terminal may end up with an adjusted level.

functions.summary: Math function returning the natural logarithm of its first argument, or the logarithm in the base given by an optional second argument.
Makes the calling actor keep its head turned toward a target reference, optionally turning the whole body as well.
notes: The forced tracking overrides normal head tracking until StopLook runs, or until the target is no longer in the loaded area.
The optional second integer (0 or 1) makes the actor turn its entire body when set.

functions.summary: Plays a named animation group on the calling actor for a given number of loops, then returns to the idle animation; optional flags select how it starts.
notes: Flag 0 lets the current animation finish its cycle before the new one starts from its beginning.
Flag 1 stops the current animation immediately and starts the new one from its beginning.
Flag 2 stops the current animation immediately and starts the new one at the beginning of its loop section.

functions.summary: Sets the delete flag on a reference so it is queued for removal a few frames later, which also stops its script from running.
notes: Runtime-created references (dropped items, PlaceAtMe results) are fully deleted; references defined in plugins are not truly removed, but their scripts stop running.
It works on enabled references too, but the object stays visible and frozen until the area is left, so disable visible ones first.
Meant for references never to be enabled again; handy for cleaning up unneeded trigger volumes.
On inventory references it can crash, and in an OnAdd block it crashes; OnActivate works but the prompt may linger. It works with items that have OnDrop blocks.
Disabled objects stay in memory and keep running scripts, which is why deletion is useful.
bugs: Marking an actor together with several objects in the same moment can cause a crash to desktop.

functions.summary: Morphs the calling actor's face geometry toward a source actor's face by a percentage from 0 to 100.
notes: 100 means identical geometry; 50 is a half morph from the current face.
Only the geometry changes, not the face texture.

functions.summary: Changes the calling actor's race to the race currently held by another actor.
notes: The affected actor receives the default face textures of the new race.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if any menu is open, or, with an integer menu type argument, if that specific menu is open, otherwise 0.
notes: Without an argument it is true whenever the game is not in normal gameplay mode.
Usable as a condition in perks and object effects, but there it may only reliably indicate whether game mode is active rather than specific menus.
In effect scripts it never returns true while the pause menu is open.
In Fallout 3 the main menu has no code of its own; only three menu codes return true (FO3).
The race, plastic surgeon and barber menus all share one menu code.

functions.summary: Permanently changes the calling actor's chosen actor value by a positive or negative amount.
notes: Meant for lasting changes; the damage and restore functions are for temporary changes.
The resulting value can go beyond the usual cap of some values, for example skills.

functions.summary: Adjusts the barter gold stored on the calling actor by the given amount.
notes: Fallout 3 merchants do not use barter gold; their caps live in the merchant container (FO3).

functions.summary: Changes the calling actor's disposition toward the specified actor by the given amount.
Adds the given amount to the calling actor's rank in a faction.
notes: Nothing happens if the actor is not in that faction.
The rank can never be lowered below 0.

functions.summary: Adjusts how one faction reacts toward a second faction by a given amount.
Applies facial expression, phoneme or modifier morphs to the calling character; takes a type, an ID and an intensity.
notes: Three kinds: expressions (full-face, one at a time), phonemes (mouth only) and modifiers (eyes and brow); a reset type clears them. Page lists the ID tables.
The effect takes a second or two to appear rather than being instant.

functions.summary: Raises or lowers one of the player's SPECIAL attributes by an amount treated as permanent, like a level-up increase.
notes: Works on SPECIAL attributes only, not skills.

functions.summary: Modifies one of the player's miscellaneous statistics, identified by its name string, by an integer amount.
notes: The page lists valid stat names separately for Fallout 3 and New Vegas.

functions.summary: Meant to add skill points that count toward leveling like earned ones, but it is unused in New Vegas and changes nothing there.
Adds the given amount to the calling reference's current scale; the argument may range from 0.5 to 2.0.
notes: The change is additive: from scale 1.2, passing 0.5 yields 1.7.

functions.summary: Adds a positive or negative amount to the condition of the weapon the calling actor currently has equipped.
notes: Negative values reduce condition.
It seems not to update the weapon's condition for the player while god mode is on.

functions.summary: Turns a chosen knob or dial on the player's Pip-Boy by a signed distance; not every knob ID is known.
Moves the calling object or actor to the position of the given marker reference, with optional X, Y and Z offsets.
notes: It can fire the object's OnLoad block, since the object is effectively unloaded and reloaded.
When moving the player, a movement request is queued; it is not immediate and the script keeps running.
Actors snap to navmesh and generally cannot be placed off it unless flagged immobile; furniture markers must be persistent to move actors onto them.
For non-actor objects the coordinates change but the visual does not; a disable, move, enable, Update3D sequence is needed. Ragdolls drop to the floor below.
Actors flagged for no low-level processing cannot return home once outside the loaded area.
bugs: Moving a container with the respawn flag makes its contents respawn immediately and again on every return to that cell.

functions.summary: Fades the calling object out, moves it to the given marker reference (with optional X, Y, Z offsets), then fades it back in.
notes: Not suited to instant moves, because it waits for the fade-out to complete.
Can be used to imitate an actor using a door.

functions.summary: Moves the player to the current Pip-Boy quest objective; an optional integer index selects among several markers of a quest.
Casts a ray from the crosshairs between a minimum and maximum range and returns the first object hit, which can be far beyond activation range.
notes: Range is capped at 50000 units; distances are in game units (128 is about 1.8 m).
Like the crosshair reference function, it also returns statics and other collidable objects, not just activatable ones, so results usually need filtering by type.
