functions.summary: Opens the teammate-style container menu, letting the player freely swap inventory with the calling actor.
notes: Optional IgnoreTeammate defaults to 0, restricting it to the player's teammates; passing 1 makes it work on any actor.

functions.summary: Writes the local map to disk as a set of PNG images, forcibly changing the grids-to-load setting so only the local area is output.
notes: Changing the grid setting can break scripted sequences, so the page advises using it for testing only.

functions.summary: Prints how many persistent references currently exist in the game.
Makes the calling actor choose and play an idle animation whose conditions currently match.
notes: Does nothing when no idle animation satisfies its conditions; the forced-idle function plays one regardless of conditions.

functions.summary: Selects a reference by ID as the current target for console commands.
Controls the Pip-Boy radio: turn off (0), turn on (1), or tune (via the tune keyword) to a station given as the broadcasting talking-activator reference.
notes: Stations are named by passing the talking activator reference that broadcasts them.
A disabled or out-of-range station cannot be chosen with tune.
Tune only works while the radio is already on; otherwise the station is unchanged and command 1 resumes the last-played station.
Command 1 without a station triggers one wrong song before the correct station resumes, so a station should always be given.
bugs: Turning the radio on without naming a station plays one incorrect song first, and the same glitch affects a tune issued right after.

functions.summary: Turns the Pip-Boy radio off.
notes: Equivalent to the radio function with command 0.

functions.summary: Spawns a number of the given object at the calling reference, with optional distance and direction offsets; for leveled actors a second optional value acts as a level modifier.
notes: The new object copies the caller's XYZ angles, so things placed at a player looking up or down will be tilted.
Scripts on the new object may not be addressable in the same frame; wait a few frames. Script variables on placed objects reset on reload or game load.
Works with leveled creature lists but not leveled items, which show an error marker.
Runtime-created actors survive cell reset unless killed (then removed after about three days); projectiles survive resets; picked-up placed items are destroyed; explosions unload after one animation.
The returned reference is reliable only for non-pickable objects; using one after pickup can crash, and the self-reference getter misbehaves on such objects.
Unneeded placed references should be disabled and marked for delete to prevent save bloat.
bugs: The distance and direction arguments have no effect; the object always lands in a safe spot near the caller.
Spawning an actor with zero health produces a living actor, so a kill call is needed.
Objects with destruction data and the disable-object flag can remain disabled after loading a save from before destruction.

functions.summary: Spawns an injured actor or item near the calling reference, at a given fraction of full health, with count and optional distance and direction.
notes: Direction values: front is 0, back 1, left 2, right 3.
When the form comes from a leveled list, this health percentage replaces the list's own health setting.

functions.summary: Places the given object at the point the crosshair is aimed at, with a count and an optional maximum distance between 1 and 50000.
notes: The minimum-distance argument is marked unused.

functions.summary: Spawns a leveled actor from a base form at the calling reference using the same options as editor placement; returns the new reference, or a null form on failure.
notes: Level modifier codes: easy 0, medium 1, hard 2, boss 3, none 4; default is 4.
If no encounter zone is given, it takes the zone of the cell where the actor is created.

functions.summary: Places a small debug box at given coordinates with floating name text visible through walls; defaults to coordinates as name, optional colour 0 to 9.
Plays a Bink video file, with optional flags for interruptability, muting game audio, pausing music and letterboxing.
notes: Defaults: interruptable 0, mute audio 1, pause music 1, letterboxed 1; filename is quoted and relative to the data video folder.
Files must be loose on disk, not inside a BSA archive.
A non-zero interruptable flag lets the player skip with escape; zero for letterbox avoids letterboxing a widescreen video on a 4:3 screen.
Playback appears to halt game time even if flags keep sounds going.

functions.summary: Condition function returning 1 if the player is in the given region, otherwise 0.
notes: Inside a child region, the parent region also tests true.
It is condition-only; the script-usable counterpart is IsPlayerInRegion.

functions.summary: Plays a named animation group on the calling reference, with an init flag controlling how the transition starts.
notes: Flag 0 lets the current animation finish then starts the new one from its start; 1 interrupts and starts from the beginning; 2 interrupts and starts at the loop point.
Some groups need conditions, e.g. combat reactions like recoil need a drawn weapon.
Some animations can leave actors misbehaving; playing the idle group with flag 1 restores normal control.
The stagger group has no animation files and does nothing; use a hit-reaction idle instead.
bugs: Certain animation groups on the player or NPCs can cause freezing, backwards running, walking through solids or inability to attack.

functions.summary: Makes the calling actor play a specified idle animation; the page recommends the forced or extended variants instead.
notes: It takes the idle's editor ID string literal, not a form reference or reference variable.
On the player it works only in fly-camera mode, or in the frame the player activated the scripted object with default activation suppressed; also via a script effect's implicit reference.
Placing the animation outside the characters folder removes those limits.
bugs: Calling it directly on the player is bugged and works only in narrow circumstances.

functions.summary: Plays a magic effect's visuals on the calling reference for an optional duration.
notes: Always runs a minimum of one cycle regardless of duration; without a duration it runs once, or indefinitely if the art keeps animating.

functions.summary: Plays an effect shader's visuals on the calling reference for an optional duration.
notes: Always runs a minimum of one cycle regardless of duration; without a duration it runs until the art stops animating.
On the player, the shader only shows in the perspective (first or third person) active when it started.
With no calling reference it defaults to the player.

functions.summary: Plays the specified music type form.
notes: It will not interrupt music already playing from a music marker (New Vegas only).

functions.summary: Plays a sound form non-positionally; a non-zero system-sound flag makes it play even in menu mode, otherwise it may be queued until game mode returns.
bugs: Does not work for ambient sounds built from OGG or MP3 files.

functions.summary: Plays a sound form positionally at the calling reference's location.
notes: Fails if the reference has no model.
The sound file must be mono for 3D playback; stereo falls back to 2D.

functions.summary: Sets the camera paths used the next time VATS playback runs to those assigned to the given path.
Queues loading of a spell effect's particles if not already loaded; does nothing if they are already loading.
notes: Only useful when a non-actor reference casts the spell, since actors preload their own spells.

functions.summary: Forcibly unloads all cells in the cell buffers that are not currently attached.
Knocks the target actor down (ragdoll) and pushes it away from the calling actor with an integer force; a negative force pulls it toward the caller.
notes: No effect on dead actors, on actors flagged immobile, or on actors with the no-knockdowns flag.
A pushed actor's inventory can be opened by the player until it gets back up.
With no calling reference, the target is launched straight up with the given force.

functions.summary: Immediately exits the game to the desktop.
Records up to 20 console commands into a text file for later replay; no argument starts or cancels recording, a filename saves it.
Lets weather return to normal dynamic behaviour after it was overridden by a set-weather or force-weather call using the override flag.
Reloads a user-interface element from its XML definition; arguments include a UI globals option, a HUD safe zone option, the main menu, or a named menu class.
Swaps every occurrence of one water type for a different water type.
Removes everything from the calling reference's inventory, moving it to an optional target container or destroying it; unplayable biped items and, for the player, quest items are exempt.
notes: With a target container, items move there and equipment keeps its condition; without one they are destroyed like RemoveItem. Without a calling container it does nothing.
A non-zero retain-ownership flag keeps the original ownership; otherwise ownership is cleared.
A third optional flag suppresses the item messages.
bugs: Calling it on the player can crash New Vegas under unknown conditions.

functions.summary: Extended RemoveAllItems that removes only items of a chosen form type, optionally skipping members of an exemption form list; unplayable biped items and player quest items are exempt.
notes: Type code omitted or -1 removes everything like RemoveAllItems, 0 removes nothing; other values are form type IDs (page has a code table).
With a target container the items move there with equipment condition kept; otherwise destroyed like RemoveItem.
A non-zero retain-ownership flag keeps original ownership, which can count as stealing when handing items to the player; otherwise ownership is cleared.
A suppress-messages flag of 1 hides the item added pop-up when transferring to the player.

functions.summary: Removes the calling actor from every faction it belongs to.
Removes the calling actor reference, not its base object, from the given faction.
notes: Differs from the faction-rank setter, which acts on the actor's base form; other instances of the same base actor stay in the faction.

functions.summary: Removes the specified imagespace modifier from the screen.
Destroys a given count of an item from the calling container's inventory, with an optional flag to suppress the on-screen message.
notes: The item argument may be a form list, in which case the count is removed for each item on the list.
Items are destroyed rather than dropped nearby.
If the removed item was equipped, its OnUnequip block does not run.

functions.summary: Removes the calling item from the container holding it; with a target container argument, a copy is moved there instead.
notes: It acts like a return: script lines after it are not executed.
Preserves health and charge; a copy moved to a target container does not retain the original's script variables; no removal message is shown.
With stacked items, the one actually removed may be the first in the stack rather than the caller.
If called in OnEquip it does not run OnUnequip.
The vanilla game only uses it inside OnAdd blocks; elsewhere it may crash, and the drop function is advised.
bugs: Called by an item inside a container that is not persistent it crashes; in a persistent container it works unless that container is the player; OnAdd use does not crash.
The removed object's GameMode block keeps running, and it still reports its old container, for an undetermined time.
Calling it in a GameMode block without a one-shot guard variable makes the game loop forever and freeze.
In the barter menu with stackable scripted items it may crash when switching from sell to buy after selling several (page doubts this applies to the GECK).

functions.summary: Clears the merchant container assigned to an actor.
Removes a note from the player's notes; takes the note form and is not called on a reference.
notes: Unlike the add-note function, it shows no message, so the player must be notified separately.

functions.summary: Removes a perk from the calling actor; on the player it removes the player's perk, or from all teammates if the optional teammates flag is non-zero.
notes: The player carries two perk lists: one for the player and one applied to all current teammates; perk requirements only gate level-up selection, not companion perks.
Perk entry points or abilities for companions should be conditioned on being a teammate or a specific ID.
In Fallout 3, calling it from an effect script on a perk with an ability entry crashes; a scripted token calling it then removing itself is the workaround (FO3).
bugs: In Fallout 3, using it in an effect script for a perk with an ability entry crashes the game (FO3).

functions.summary: Clears the recurring flag of a challenge so it will not restart; a completed challenge becomes greyed out on the challenges screen.
Removes preset-sized reputation, fame or infamy, from a faction; despite the page summary saying adds, it subtracts.
notes: First integer picks infamy (0) or fame (1); second picks magnitude 1 to 5, mapped through game settings (defaults 1, 2, 4, 7, 12 points).
For arbitrary amounts use the exact variant.

functions.summary: Removes an exact, possibly fractional, amount of fame or infamy from a faction's reputation.
notes: First argument selects infamy (0) or fame (1), then the exact amount.
Intended for forgiveness events, not for punishing the player; infamy should be added for bad deeds.

functions.summary: Removes the script package currently running on the calling actor, so it picks a new package; needed only for packages added to run indefinitely.
notes: With no script package present it can stop the package on every instance of that actor and blocks function-triggered behaviours such as fleeing; it cancels one a function started.
A parameter is accepted by the compiler but ignored at runtime.
It cannot remove editor-assigned packages.
bugs: Running a package evaluation within a few frames of removal may re-add the package.

functions.summary: Removes an actor effect from the calling actor; in the vanilla game only addictions and abilities are such effects.
bugs: The page marks it deprecated because of inconsistent behaviour; the dispel function is recommended instead.

functions.summary: Runs a render stress test over the cell the player is in, warning about points where geometry, triangle, render pass or light counts exceed thresholds.
Clears saved animation and Havok state for a reference, mainly to reset triggered traps.
notes: It does not restore a moved object's world position.

functions.summary: Wipes all of an actor's current AI behaviours, after which combat, pathing and packages are evaluated afresh.
notes: A drastic command; re-evaluating the package is usually enough.
Packages added by script are stopped and removed.

functions.summary: Clears all variables changed during hacking, resetting terminals as if never hacked.
Clears variables altered by topics and conversations, resetting dialogue as if it never occurred.
notes: Currently resets the say-once and say-once-per-day flags.

functions.summary: Resets the fall damage timer so the calling object takes damage as though it had just started falling.
bugs: The page says the function is broken.

functions.summary: Restores the calling actor's health and cures crippled limbs.
Marks the given interior cell as expired.
notes: It only flags the cell as expired and performs no cleanup.
Unlike a time-based reset, the scripted version does not revive actors.
bugs: Actors are not revived by a scripted interior reset, unlike a normal timed reset.

functions.summary: Resets the calling reference's inventory, discarding all earlier added, removed or computed contents.
Must be called after the player equips a Pip-Boy for its menus to work; it also resets its external appearance, turning off an active light glow.
notes: Without it the Pip-Boy behaves like an NPC's, with no inventory, stats or data access.

functions.summary: Resets everything tied to a quest: clears stages and objectives, clears quest variables, and returns stage on/off state to defaults.
notes: The once-only and once-per-day response flags on the quest's dialogue are not cleared.

functions.summary: Sets the player's experience points back to zero; not called on a reference.
notes: The base game uses it in the character revision script triggered on leaving Goodsprings.

functions.summary: Heals damage on an actor value by raising its damage modifier toward zero by the given (possibly fractional) amount.
notes: The damage modifier is zero or negative and never rises above zero, so restoring an undamaged value changes nothing.
Accepts floating point amounts.

functions.summary: Brings the calling actor back from dead or unconscious state; an integer selects whether the revival uses an animation.
notes: Argument 1 makes the actor use an animation to stand up; 0 skips animation and the actor is simply standing.
With the animate flag set, body data is not refreshed, giving living actors with missing limbs; they reappear in VATS and cannot be removed again.
For such actors the limb-gone check always reports 1, gibs follow their source actor, behaviour ignores the missing limbs, and a weapon on a removed limb is not drawn.
Calling with animate false can crash Fallout 3 (FO3).
bugs: With animation enabled the actor falls through geometry unless resurrected in the same frame as death.

functions.summary: Stops script processing from that line onward, including all later blocks of the script.
notes: In a block that runs every frame, such as GameMode, the script runs again next frame; useful inside conditionals to skip later lines.
Cannot be used inside While or ForEach loops.

functions.summary: Adds an integer amount of karma to the player, or removes it if negative; not called on a reference.
notes: Result is clamped by the karma maximum and minimum game settings.
A corner message announces the change.

functions.summary: Awards an integer amount of experience points to the player; not called on a reference.
notes: A message normally appears stating the experience gained.

functions.summary: Rotates the calling object about the world X, Y or Z axis at a speed in degrees per second.
notes: Unreliable for complex or repeated rotations; animation functions are better for those.
Only one axis can rotate per frame per reference; repeated calls in a frame apply only the last.
Collision is not updated until the cell reloads or Update3D is used.
bugs: Often makes the object vanish when loading a save from before the call, though sometimes the change persists.

functions.summary: Returns 1 if the calling actor and the target actor share at least one faction, otherwise 0.
Returns 1 if the calling actor belongs to any faction the player also belongs to.
Yields 1 when the calling actor and the target actor share a race, otherwise 0.
Returns 1 if the calling actor has the same race as the player.
Yields 1 when the calling actor and the target actor are of one gender, otherwise 0.
Yields 1 when the calling actor has the player's gender.
Creates a named savegame and can optionally write a dump file of the save information.
Makes the calling actor speak a single dialogue line from a topic, with optional flags for forced subtitles, speaker actor, 2D playback and voice.
bugs: Inside a package result script it makes the package stall when the player is absent from the cell.
Inside a dialogue result script it may hang the game.

functions.summary: Makes the calling actor speak one dialogue line to a target actor; always returns 0, and a SayToDone block fires when the line finishes.
notes: Optional flags force subtitles and stop the target from being made to look at the speaker.
The SayToDone block is the way to react when the line completes.
bugs: Inside a package result script it makes the package stall when the player is absent from the cell.

functions.summary: Effect-script-only function returning seconds since the previous magic effect update, as a float.
notes: Gives a value above 0 only in a ScriptEffectUpdate block, though it compiles in other blocks.

functions.summary: Manually creates an assault crime, with optional victim actor and faction arguments.
notes: The player is always treated as the criminal, so it cannot make AI actors attack each other.
If the player is given as victim (not a valid target), an actor from the supplied faction is chosen instead.
Actors shout the assault dialogue topic even if already fighting the target.
bugs: Using it with no calling reference can sometimes crash the game.

functions.summary: Raises a trespass alarm as though someone reported the player trespassing; the optional argument is whoever is told.
notes: Appears to accept only the player as the offender.
Reaches the fully trespassed state in one call, regardless of the guard warnings setting.

functions.summary: Sets the transparency (alpha) of the calling actor.
notes: Does not affect the weapon the actor carries.

functions.summary: Changes the calling actor's display name to the title of the given message form.
notes: It alters the base object's name, so every instance of that actor or creature gets the new name.
Also works on talking activators.

functions.summary: Sets the essential state of only the calling actor reference, leaving the base untouched; the change is saved with the game.
notes: Cannot clear essential status if the base is essential via the editor or the base-level set-essential function.

functions.summary: Sets an actor's refraction value between 0 and 10, defaulting to the player when no reference is given; persists for the session.
Turns an actor's processing off (0) or on (any other integer); scripts still run but packages, detection, Havok and animation do not process.
Sets the base value of an actor value on the calling actor to a new integer value.
Sets whether the calling actor is in an alert animation state (weapon drawn), without altering actual combat status.
notes: The state is saved with the game and is not cleared by time or cell reset.
Combining it with unequip calls in the same moment can leave the actor holding an invisible weapon.

functions.summary: Performance aid: while the flag is set, actors skip line-of-sight checks and assume they can see a target's head.
notes: The flag is reset every frame, so it must be called repeatedly from a script on a reference within the loaded area.

functions.summary: Sets a friend or ally relationship between two factions, adding the second to the first's reaction list if missing; not called on a reference.
notes: Optional flags for each direction: 0 means ally (default), 1 means friend.

functions.summary: Sets the calling object's rotation, in degrees, about the world X, Y or Z axis.
notes: On the player and actors only Z rotation turns them; X and Y tilt has no effect, except that X on the player pitches the camera.
The player's X angle can exceed mouse limits (about -89 to 89); negative values look up, positive look down.
Some objects keep snapping X back to zero within a few frames; statics may only respond if spawned dynamically.

functions.summary: Assigns the barter gold amount held by an actor; effectively unused.
notes: Fallout 3 merchants do not use barter gold; their caps are placed in their container (FO3).

functions.summary: Switches a radio station's broadcast mode: 0 stops continuous broadcast, 1 starts it.
notes: State 0 plays static except for scripted radio conversations; state 1 plays generated radio conversations back to back.

functions.summary: Sets the world and first-person field of view; either argument omitted or 0 gives the default of 75.
notes: Both values are capped at 160.
A negative value is turned into the reciprocal of its absolute value.
World FOV controls how close the world seems; first-person FOV controls how close the player's hands and gear look.

functions.summary: Sets the winnings level, an integer from 0 to 4, of a casino.
Changes a cell's display name to the title text of the given message form, affecting load door labels and the local map.
notes: Works only for interior cells.

functions.summary: Changes the imagespace assigned to a cell.
notes: On a currently loaded cell the new imagespace is not applied until the cell reloads, such as after leaving and returning or loading a save made there.

functions.summary: Sets a cell's owner to the given NPC or faction base form; with no second argument the player becomes the owner.
Sets a cell's public flag to 1 or 0; public cells cannot have trespassing, so this changes crime behaviour in the cell.
Changes the calling actor's class to the given class form, running autocalc only if the actor has autocalc enabled.
Overrides the far clip distance while in interior cells.
notes: In an exterior the override is dropped at once.

functions.summary: Sets the cost of a named combat action; a higher cost makes the AI less likely to choose it.
Assigns a new combat style form to the calling actor reference.
notes: Changes only the calling reference, not the combat style on the actor's base form.

functions.summary: Creates a text file that logs console input and output.
Puts the calling reference into the given critical stage (none, goo start/end, disintegrate start/end) and applies its effects.
notes: Start stages change the ragdoll constraints; end stages finalise it by dropping it from water handling, removing its rendered 3D, and discarding its physics data.

functions.summary: Sets the default open state of the calling object, matching the open-by-default option on a placed reference.
Sets the destroyed flag on the calling reference (1) or clears it (0).
notes: Destroyed doors and activators give no rollover text and cannot be activated.
Avoid on temporary references, since the flag seems to persist if the form ID is reused; not recommended on actors; avoid on spawn markers.
bugs: On spawn markers it causes assorted bugs, including immunity to explosives.
On temporary references the flag may not clear when the form ID is reused.

functions.summary: Sets the calling actor's disposition toward the given actor to an integer value.
Sets an enemy or neutral relationship between two factions, adding the second to the first's reaction list if missing; not called on a reference.
notes: Optional flags for each direction: 0 means enemy (default), 1 means neutral.

functions.summary: Sets the essential state of an actor's base form by its base ID, with a boolean flag.
Sets the calling actor's rank within a faction, joining the faction at that rank if not already a member; a negative rank removes the actor from it.
notes: Rank argument is optional.
The rank is written to the actor's base object as well as the reference, so later actors spawned from that base already carry the faction and rank.
bugs: Because the rank lives on the base object, random unnamed actors or creatures sharing a base all inherit the faction membership.

functions.summary: Sets how one faction regards a target faction to the given amount.
Turns forced running on or off for the calling actor.
Turns forced sneaking on or off for the calling actor.
bugs: When toggled back and forth in quick succession by a script not attached to the affected actor, the actor's visible sneak state can disagree with what IsSneaking and GetForceSneak report.
With force sneak on, an actor firing via FireWeapon stands up, because animation groups fail to refresh.

functions.summary: Sets a named game setting to a new value; numeric or string depending on the setting.
Puts the calling actor into or out of the ghost state, which makes it unharmable; the change persists in saves.
notes: Ghosts take no damage from weapons or magic effects, and projectiles pass through them.
A ghost can still deal damage, talk, be activated for dialog, and collides normally with actors and world objects.
Enemies of a ghost do not detect it or enter combat with it.
Pickpocketing a ghost is impossible; ordinary activation (dialog) happens instead.
Applied to the player, it does not stop the player taking damage.
bugs: The VATS hit chance shown for a ghost is unchanged even though it cannot be hit.
The pickpocket prompt still appears for a ghost despite pickpocketing being impossible.

functions.summary: Sets the global time scale (1.0 normal, lower is slow motion), optionally leaving sound pitch/speed unaffected.
notes: Second parameter is optional and defaults to 0; when 1, sounds are not sped up or slowed with the time change.
Passing a multiplier of 0 breaks the game.
bugs: A multiplier of 0 breaks the game.

functions.summary: Turns hardcore mode on (1) or off (0).
notes: Reportedly has no effect when the player is the calling reference; calling it from an OnTrigger block with the trigger as reference is suggested.
bugs: Calling it on the player appears to do nothing.

functions.summary: Sets the HUD glow parameters: blur radius, blur intensity and scanline frequency.
notes: All three float parameters are optional.

functions.summary: Sets or clears a flag making the calling actor ignore hits from friendly sources.
Puts the player into or out of character-generation state, in which level-ups are withheld.
notes: While in this state XP still accumulates but no level is gained.
On leaving the state, all earned levels are awarded at once.

functions.summary: Sets an INI setting to a new value, identified by a setting-name and category string.
notes: The setting string has the form SettingName:CategoryName, where the category is the INI section header.

functions.summary: Sets the base value of the calling item reference's base object, so every reference to that base changes value.
notes: The change is stored in save games.

functions.summary: Sets which exterior door counts as the last one activated.
notes: Changes which worldspace map the Pip-Boy shows.
The worldspace that owns the cell now loaded is left as it was.

functions.summary: Sets an actor's level; when the level-to-player flag is on, the level acts as an offset from the player's level within optional min and max bounds.
notes: Min and max level arguments are optional.
On non-player actors it regenerates the inventory, re-evaluating leveled lists, even if the level did not change.
On the player it alters the level number but no stats, and the world does not scale; granting XP is preferred.
bugs: On NPCs it often sets the level to the minimum level, ignoring the offset and the maximum.

functions.summary: Restricts load screens to those tied specifically to the current cell when set to 1.
Sets the anisotropic filtering level.
notes: Page lists six accepted levels, from 1 up to 16; any other value rounds down to the closest lower level.

functions.summary: Assigns a merchant container reference to the calling actor.
notes: Fails if the container reference is not persistent.

functions.summary: Sets or clears the minimal-use flag on the calling door.
Overrides the default sound played when activation is refused with a specified sound.
notes: ClearNoActivationSound restores the default.

functions.summary: Performance switch that, when enabled, makes actors skip avoid-box movement.
notes: The flag resets each frame, so a script attached to something in the loaded area must keep re-applying it.
When set, actors neither open doors nor angle away from each other.

functions.summary: Makes the calling NPC act as a radio playing a given radio station reference, or switches that off.
notes: A first 0/1 parameter turns the radio off or on; 0 turns it off regardless of the station given.
If the NPC is the speaker of a dialog line it speaks it normally; otherwise the line plays with a filter effect.
To change the station, the radio must first be turned off, then on with the new station.

functions.summary: Marks a quest objective as completed or not completed.
notes: An Objective Completed message appears only when the objective is on display and its quest has not itself been completed.
If the quest is already complete no message appears, though the objective is still marked.
Completed objectives that are displayed show greyed out in the interface.

functions.summary: Turns a quest objective's display on or off.
notes: The first displayed objective of a quest triggers a Quest Added message.
Displaying an objective starts the quest if it is not running.
Only indices defined on the quest's objectives list work; undefined indices do nothing.

functions.summary: Opens or closes the calling door.
notes: The states used do not correspond to those returned by GetOpenState.
Also works on activators that have open and close animations.

functions.summary: Sets the calling reference's owner to an NPC or faction base form; with no argument the player becomes owner.
notes: Owner argument is optional and defaults to the player's base form.

functions.summary: Sets how long the actor's current AI package runs, in minutes of game time.
notes: Useful for packages that should last less than an hour.

functions.summary: Sets the flag that lets the player use power armor.
notes: The power armor training perk is only a display dummy; the real flag is set by a stage of a generic quest.

functions.summary: Sets or clears the flag marking the player as an enemy of a crime-tracking faction after a major crime.
Expels the player from a faction and sets the expelled flag, or clears the flag when the second argument is 0.
notes: If the player is inside a cell owned by that faction, they are moved outside through the nearest door.

functions.summary: Forces the player to sleep for the given number of hours.
Switches the player to the toddler walk animation set (1) or back to normal (0).
Flags the player as young, which limits the player to the race's default hair and suppresses loading of face attachments.
Assigns a named skill as the player's tag skill at index 0 to 3, granting the starting tag bonus in that skill.
notes: The game supports at most four tagged skills; indices above 3 appear to do nothing.
Tagging extra skills through SetTagSkills or AddTagSkills beyond four has no effect past the first four.

functions.summary: Makes the calling actor behave as the player's combat teammate (1) or clears it (0), so others treat it as in the player faction.
notes: Increments the player teammate count; the state is cleared on the actor's death and the count decremented.
Teammate imitates the player's sneak state and can be activated during combat.
Changing cells teleports the teammate to the player.
Enables OpenTeammateContainer, even when the parameter is 1.
Enables the companion wheel and shows a Pip-Boy map marker for the teammate (New Vegas).
In Hardcore mode a teammate flagged essential loses that protection (New Vegas).

functions.summary: Sets the calling object's world position along one chosen axis (X, Y or Z).
notes: MoveTo is recommended for placing objects in remote cells.
Works on activators, but static, static collection, tree, flora and furniture forms are unaffected unless dynamically spawned, e.g. via PlaceAtMe.
Moving an object that supports dynamic navmesh cutting leaves the cutout stale until Update3D is called.

functions.summary: Sets how often the quest's scripts are processed, in seconds; the change is stored in saves.
notes: Default interval is 5 seconds, taken from an INI setting.
A delay of 0 restores the INI default interval.
Short delays should be used only temporarily for a specific purpose, then reset to the default, to avoid wasting processing time.

functions.summary: Sets or clears the quest-item flag on a form (object or actor).
notes: Flagged NPCs and creatures get update priority when the player changes process state, following through load doors faster, and corpses are not cleaned up on cell expiry.
Flagged inventory items cannot be dropped or sold by the player.
Only some form types can be quest items: talking activator, armor, book, misc, weapon, ammo, NPC, creature, key, ingestible and weapon mod.

functions.summary: Puts the Pip-Boy radio into dialogue-only mode (1) or out of it (0).
Sets the player's fame or infamy with a reputation form to an exact amount, replacing the previous value.
notes: The second argument selects fame versus infamy.

functions.summary: Sets or clears a restrained state in which the actor stays in place and does not enter combat but still thinks and can talk.
notes: Restrained actors still pick packages and run detection, so they can raise alarms, and they still go into dialogue.
Also blocks weapon use from Use Weapon packages and UseWeapon; the actor tries the package and animations but never attacks.

functions.summary: Sets an object's mass, controlling how much it moves when bumped or hit.
notes: Valid values are 0 to 100, where 100 means it does not move at all.

functions.summary: Sets controller rumble using left motor strength, right motor strength and a duration.
notes: Duration is in seconds.

functions.summary: Sets the calling object's scale, with 1.0 as normal size; the change is stored in saves.
notes: A scale of 0 can pseudo-disable an item while its OnLoad block still runs.
Actor weight follows scale, so smaller actors are easier to carry.
Movement speed and damage also vary with scale.
Visual update is often delayed until the cell is reloaded or a save is loaded; Update3D forces it.
bugs: On dead actors GetScale updates but the body size does not until ResurrectActor, or Disable then Enable.

functions.summary: Enables a simplified-processing mode for scenes with many combatants; the flag clears every frame so must be reapplied each frame.
notes: Flag is wiped every frame, so a script attached to a load door or activator in the loaded area must keep setting it.
Reduces animation and sound detail, omits disposition checks for actors already fighting when deciding whether to attack, and combat ignores movement restrictions.
Low and middle-low process levels stop updating, so actors outside the loaded area freeze and cannot pass through load doors.
Surplus corpses nearby are removed more frequently, and avoidance is switched off.

functions.summary: Sets the monitor expression of a Securitron reference using a face name and an expression name.
notes: Persists across saves and restarts.
Works from texture filenames in the Securitron creature textures folder, named face then underscore then expression, so custom faces need matching files.

functions.summary: Shows (1, default) or hides (0) quest items in the player's inventory.
notes: Hiding must be used carefully, since the player could permanently lose access to quest items.

functions.summary: Sets the calling actor's collision radius to the given size, with 0.0 restoring the original radius.
notes: The value becomes the radius of the actor's collision box.
bugs: Unreliable or ineffective for non-player actors.

functions.summary: Sets the sky's sunlight dimmer and luminance ramp values.
Opens the character-generation attributes page so the player can distribute SPECIAL points up to a specified total.
notes: The argument is the total SPECIAL points the player will have after leaving the menu, not a delta.
If it exceeds the current total the player may add the difference; if lower, the player must remove the difference.

functions.summary: Marks a quest stage as done and runs its qualifying stage items: results, log entries, and quest completion where applicable.
notes: Starts the quest automatically if it is not running.
First stage added to the Pip-Boy triggers a Quest Added message.
Does nothing if the quest has no such stage index.
Called from the new-game quest it exits the main menu, moving from menu mode to game mode.
Stage result scripts run immediately and halt the calling script until finished; SetStage may be nested inside result scripts, with at least 250 levels of recursion working.

functions.summary: Opens the character-generation skills page to let the player choose tagged skills up to a given total.
notes: The first argument is the total number of tags to be selected, not an increment.
Optional second argument defaults to 1; at 0, the player's existing tag skills are hidden and can be overwritten.
Only the first four tagged skills take effect, even if more are chosen here or via AddTagSkills.

functions.summary: Makes a talking activator (such as a computer) use the dialogue of a given actor; with no actor it reverts to normal behaviour.
notes: Actor argument is optional; omitting it restores the activator's own voice and dialogue.
Talking activators configured by script have no distance attenuation in New Vegas.

functions.summary: Changes the speed multiplier of the player's camera, mainly when detached with the fly camera.
Turns an actor's conscious behaviour off (1) or on (0); unconscious actors run no AI and make no idle sounds.
notes: Activating an unconscious actor shows a message saying it is unconscious.
Used on a dead actor it resurrects it without a get-up animation, and like ResurrectActor can cause animation problems unless called in the frame of death.

functions.summary: Enables or disables VATS targetability of the calling destructible object, taking precedence over the base object's own setting.
Sets the velocity of a reference along a chosen axis.
Sets the condition percentage of the actor's currently equipped weapon.
notes: New Vegas hard-limits the result so condition never rises above 99.83 percent, a workaround for a calculation problem at exactly full condition.
bugs: Condition cannot be raised past 99.83 percent in New Vegas.

functions.summary: Switches to the given weather using the normal transition, optionally overriding the weather system until the override is released.
notes: Transition time depends on the weather's transition-delta setting, or on SetWeatherTransitionTimeOverride if that was used.
Optional override flag: if 1, weather stays until ReleaseWeatherOverride is called; otherwise it reverts to the normal weather cycle.

functions.summary: Turns respawning on or off for an encounter zone; the change is stored in saves.
notes: Respawn interval for zones is governed by the game setting for hours to respawn a cell (default 72 hours).

functions.summary: Changes an actor's gender to a given sex, or flips it if none is given; with no calling reference it affects the player.
notes: Both parameters are optional: target sex, and a reset-appearance flag defaulting to 0.
Reset-appearance applies only if the actor is the player and the sex really changes; the appearance then becomes the default preset for that race and gender.
An NPC whose hair is invalid for the new sex gets the default hair.

functions.summary: Prints the value of a special or global variable.
Shows the first-person model while using the third-person camera, showing both in third-person mode.
Shows or removes every map marker on the world map, with optional arguments for fast travel and for leaving out hidden-flagged markers.
notes: Second and third arguments (can travel, skip hidden) are optional and default to 1.
Removing markers (first argument 0) also removes hidden-flagged ones in the page's example, and hiding markers turns off travel for them regardless of the travel argument.
Showing with travel 0 does not disable fast travel on markers already enabled for it.
If the Pip-Boy is open, the map does not refresh until it is closed and reopened.

functions.summary: Shows animation and actor status information for the calling reference.
Opens the menu where the player picks hair colour and style; takes no parameters.
Opens the barter menu with the calling actor as vendor, optionally applying a percentage discount or markup to prices.
notes: Optional parameter ranges from -100 to 100 and gives a percent discount on sell prices and inflation on buy prices.
Default is 0, meaning no price change.

functions.summary: Opens the blackjack menu for a casino form, with optional minimum bet, maximum bet and maximum winnings.
notes: The menu only appears if casino requirements are met, such as having casino chips and not being banned.
Bet and winnings arguments are optional.

functions.summary: Starts a caravan card game with the calling NPC using a given deck, difficulty level and maximum bet fraction of their currency.
notes: Arguments are deck, difficulty (0 to 3 per the page) and maximum bet as a fraction of the opponent's currency.
Maximum currency for both player and opponent counts the base value of all faction currency held.

functions.summary: Opens the interface of the calling terminal reference; a locked terminal skips the hacking minigame.
bugs: Crashes the game if the calling reference is missing or not a terminal.

functions.summary: Builds the full scene graph tree and expands the node of the selected item.
Opens the calling terminal reference with the hacking minigame.
bugs: Crashes the game if the calling reference is missing or not a terminal.

functions.summary: Lists the contents of a targeted reference with counts, IDs and worn status, plus condition values for weapons and armor.
Opens the lockpicking interface, with an optional difficulty level.
notes: Optional difficulty has five levels from very easy to very hard; default is the middle, average level.

functions.summary: Opens the lockpick menu plus a debug display of sweet spot and pick health, with an optional lock level.
notes: Lock level is optional, from very easy at 0 upward; the page is inconsistent about the upper limit (5 in text, 6 in the argument table).

functions.summary: Opens the Vigor Tester menu so the player can distribute or redistribute SPECIAL points.
notes: Argument gives the full pool of SPECIAL points the player may allocate.

functions.summary: Adds a map marker to the world map, optionally enabling fast travel to it.
notes: Optional second argument enables fast travel; when omitted, the marker is added without fast travel.

functions.summary: Displays a message form to the player, optionally inserting up to nine variable values into its text.
notes: Number of variable arguments must equal the number of format specifiers in the message; a wrong count makes the message fail to display.
Variable arguments must be declared variables or globals, not constants, and cannot be placed in button text.
Message type picks a non-interrupting HUD message or a message box that pauses the game until a button is pressed; buttonless boxes get OK.
Text supports printf-style float formats with width and flags, scientific notation, a literal percent sign, and control-key name insertion.
Use GetButtonPressed to detect which button was chosen.
bugs: The trailing Duration parameter has no effect.
Showing a message from a MenuMode block in reaction to a button on an on-screen message can fail to appear; using a GameMode block is advised.
The general number format switches to scientific notation at one million and above.

functions.summary: Opens the menu where the player changes their name.
notes: Menu text comes from the enter-name game setting.

functions.summary: Opens the menu where the player changes their face; takes no parameters.
Lists the player's currently running quests.
Lists every stage of a quest along with whether each has been set.
Reports the active quest's current targets, with each target's reference and load door.
Lists the script variables of a given quest.
Opens the race menu (Gene Projector in FO3, Reflectron in New Vegas) for choosing sex, race, face and hair; takes no parameters.
notes: Changing race in this menu removes the player's ability and temporary actor effects.

functions.summary: Opens the crafting recipe menu for a given recipe category, called on an actor or activator.
Opens the repair menu so equipment can be repaired for caps, using the calling actor's repair skill.
notes: Caps paid go into the calling actor's inventory.
Called with no reference it compiles but does nothing.
On the player, spent caps return to the player's inventory, yet the player needs enough caps before repairing.

functions.summary: Opens the roulette menu for a casino form, with optional minimum bet, maximum bet and maximum winnings.
notes: The menu only appears if casino requirements are met, such as having casino chips and not being banned.

functions.summary: Opens a window with the full scene graph, or just the selected reference's graph.
Opens the wait or sleep menu, with an optional flag to check sleep/wait preconditions.
notes: First argument chooses wait (0) or sleep (1); second argument is optional and defaults to false.
Some game settings control the text displayed by the menu.
bugs: When the precondition flag is 1, the first argument is ignored and the sleep menu always opens, if preconditions pass.

functions.summary: Opens the slot machine menu for a casino form, with optional minimum bet, maximum bet and maximum winnings.
notes: The menu only appears if casino requirements are met, such as having casino chips and not being banned.

functions.summary: Opens the SPECIAL book menu so the player can distribute or redistribute SPECIAL points.
notes: Argument gives the full pool of SPECIAL points the player may allocate.

functions.summary: Opens the traits menu for the player to choose traits.
notes: How many traits can be chosen is set by a game setting for the trait menu maximum.

functions.summary: Displays a message form as a message box in the manual-book visual style.
Shows all variable names and values of an object.
Prints assorted debug information about the calling reference.
Writes a warning message string to the warnings log, useful for debugging script flow.
notes: Also pops up a message box unless the user chose the yes-to-all option on an earlier warning.

functions.summary: Returns the sine of an angle given in degrees, or with the optional arc flag the arcsine in degrees.
notes: Optional second argument selects the arcsine form.

functions.summary: Returns the square root of a value.
notes: Math functions like this, especially pow and log, are slow and should not run in per-frame blocks.

functions.summary: Outputs the IDs of the currently displayed menu stack.
Starts every quest in the game.
Makes the calling actor the victim of a cannibalism act by a given actor, who regains some health.
notes: Cannibalizing is a hostile act.
Works on living actors too, which can look odd since the animation is meant for corpses.

functions.summary: Forces the calling actor to start combat with a target actor, or with the target's combat group if it is already fighting.
notes: Has no effect when the caller belongs to a faction that makes it friendly or allied toward the target.
Combat state is not always immediate; unless the target is visible, the caller searches toward its position.
The search aborts if the target is too far or evades detection too long, returning the caller to non-hostile (if it was not hostile before).

functions.summary: Forces the calling NPC to seek out a target actor and start a conversation, optionally with a chosen topic; targeting the player makes the NPC force-greet.
notes: Topic argument is optional and replaces the normal greeting topic when given, so dialogue can open on any topic.
Optional speaker and target location references presumably help pathing, e.g. across cell transitions.
Optional flags (1 or 0) enable head tracking and movement during the conversation.
The caller walks to the target wherever they are.
If either actor is disabled, nothing happens.
bugs: If the NPC is in combat with the player, it opens with the greeting topic instead of the chosen one.

functions.summary: Starts a quest, enabling its dialogue and beginning its quest script if there is one.
bugs: Starting an already running quest should be avoided: its script variables reset to 0 when a saved game is reloaded.

functions.summary: Triggers a conversation on the calling radio station, optionally beginning with a specific topic; otherwise normal conversation rules choose.
notes: If the station is broadcasting, the conversation interrupts it and looping broadcasts then resume.
If the station is not broadcasting, the single conversation plays and broadcasting stays off, so the broadcast state is unchanged.

functions.summary: Ends the calling actor's combat state so it stops fighting.
notes: The actor can return to combat if it has low disposition or stays aggressive toward nearby actors.
Most useful for actors placed in combat by StartCombat; StopCombatAlarmOnActor is the alternative to stop every enemy of one actor.

functions.summary: Clears the fighting flag on every enemy targeting the calling actor, returning them to normal routines.
notes: Forcefully affects all hostile actors and creatures aimed at the actor; StopCombat handles a single actor.

functions.summary: Cancels forced head tracking set by Look so the actor goes back to normal head tracking.
Stops playing the visuals of a given magic effect on the calling reference.
Stops a given effect shader playing on the calling actor.
notes: No need to stop a shader that was started with a duration.
Particle shaders using full particle birth count are not forcibly halted; only those using persistent particle count are stopped.

functions.summary: Stops a quest, disabling its dialogue and halting its script after the current iteration.
notes: Called from the quest's own script it does not act like a return; the script runs to the end of the last block.

functions.summary: Returns an actor to normal package behaviour after it was put into the wait state by Wait.
Replaces the texture on a named NIF block of a reference with a new texture path.
notes: Texture path omits any data or textures folder prefix and the file extension.
Block name need not start with the double hash unless the block's real name does.
Not saved: unloading the reference or loading a save reverts altered textures to their originals.
bugs: An invalid texture or path either does nothing or turns that block pink.

functions.summary: Creates a single special system save, shown only in the load list and overwritten by each later call.
notes: The base game calls it only just before the player can start the Hoover Dam battle.

functions.summary: Returns the tangent of an angle given in degrees, or with the optional arc flag the arctangent in degrees.
notes: Optional second argument selects the arctangent form.

functions.summary: Runs a render test over cells, controlled by an optional mode argument.
notes: Optional status argument starts or stops testing and picks which cells to cover; the page lists the values.
Cells with navmesh are sampled above each triangle; cells without are sampled at each reference's bound center.
At each sample point it renders eight compass directions looking level, up and down, and warns when geometry, triangle, render-pass or light counts exceed thresholds.

functions.summary: Reports memory usage for the current cell.
Opens the race menu (Gene Projector in FO3, Reflectron in New Vegas), equivalent to ShowRaceMenu.
Toggles the calling actor's AI on and off.
Toggles culling of one cell scene node chosen by ID.
notes: The page lists seven node IDs, covering actor, marker, land, static, dynamic, multibound and water nodes.

functions.summary: Toggles collision detection, letting the player float and pass through walls and ceilings when off.
Like god mode but without unlimited ammo.
Toggles whether actors are able to detect each other.
notes: An actor already in combat when detection is toggled stays in combat until it is toggled again.

functions.summary: Disables or enables facial emotions on all actors.
Toggles the free-fly debug camera, with an optional mode selecting one of three behaviours.
notes: Mode 1 freezes the game fully while the camera moves freely.
Mode 2 freezes everything including the display, showing the last rendered frame until exit.
Mode 3 freezes the camera pose for occlusion and accumulation, with a free camera, while the game keeps running.

functions.summary: Switches fog of war on the local map on or off.
Makes the player immune to damage, free of AP cost in VATS and free of ammo use.
Toggles rendering of grass on an exterior cell's terrain.
Disables or enables the leaves of all speedtrees.
Toggles a bright-lights mode that ignores cell lighting and brightens everything.
Disables or enables the display of all LOD.
Disables or enables actors turning their heads to face other actors.
Toggles debug output when a spell is applied to an actor, covering resistance, invalid targets and per-effect magnitude and duration values.
Toggles a colour-coded view of material geometry around objects with material data.
notes: The page lists the display colour for each material type.

functions.summary: Hides or shows all menus and HUD elements.
Toggles a display of navmesh in game.
bugs: Crashes the game in the unmodified game.

functions.summary: Toggles a colour-coded display of primitive shapes, for example trigger volumes.
bugs: Most of the original rendering code was removed, so release builds draw only spheres.

functions.summary: Shows the refraction render target in the top-left corner of the screen.
notes: The preview only appears when a refraction shader is in the camera's view.

functions.summary: Disables or enables all scripts.
Turns sky effects on or off; with them off the horizon is dull grey or black.
Disables or enables the animated parts of all speedtrees.
notes: Only animated portions such as leaves are affected, not the whole tree.

functions.summary: Disables or enables water rendering.
notes: The effect is not permanent; water renders again on entering it or when seen from certain angles.

functions.summary: Shows the world as wireframe.
Manually triggers the screen-blur hit effect normally used when the player staggers, with a given strength.
notes: Strength has no hard upper bound but values above about 4 or 5 lose the intended effect.

functions.summary: Triggers a shudder effect on the HUD, using four optional float parameters for intensity and duration.
notes: All four float arguments are optional.

functions.summary: Shows a screen blood effect that fades slowly; the count sets the amount.
notes: Count ranges from 1 to 100, a higher count showing more blood.

functions.summary: Forces the calling actor to unequip an item, with optional flags to block re-equipping and to hide the unequip message.
notes: If the no-equip flag is 1, the actor cannot equip the item until it is equipped via EquipItem.
If the hide-message flag is 1, the unequipped message is not shown.
Does not fire the OnUnequip script event; UnequipItemAlt does.
The no-equip flag is effectively ignored by companions, who re-equip the item if it is their best option.
bugs: On the player with the inventory open, the equipped indicator updates immediately only if the hide-message flag is 0; otherwise it lags until another graphic refreshes.

functions.summary: Unlocks the calling terminal or lock.
notes: Player gets access regardless of lock level or an earlier lockout.

functions.summary: Enables a challenge that was flagged to start disabled so it can progress on the challenges screen.
Sets the content of an open book menu to a workbook HTML file in the menus folder.
Makes the calling actor use a weapon from a given spot against a target for a number of shots, with optional behaviour flags.
notes: Required arguments: weapon, where to stand, target, number of shots.
Optional flags: crouch to reload and hold fire when blocked both default true.
Optional always-hit (for scripted kills) and no-damage (for fake combat) default false.
Optional last argument restricts where the target must stand; default or null means anywhere.
